`text % value` was refused in words by ADR 0215, and the refusal was right: a compiled text is an index into
`@str_tab`, so treating `%` as a remainder there printed `0.0` for CPython's `3.50` — the answer Gap R.165
filed and ADR 0282 closed with a guard. Building the door (ADR 0360) meant *retiring* four artefacts of that
honest period, not just deleting one `return`: the capability row that said the operator does not exist, the
CLI test that asserted `print("%.2f" % 3.5)` exits 1, the conformance row that said **both** legs refuse, and
the probe program written to prove refusal. Each of them was correct on the day it was written and each one
would have been a lie after the door landed, and a lie that a green suite certifies is worse than a red one.
The general rule: when a feature lands, `git grep` the refusals it retires — the tests, the registry, the
docs and the ledger — before the suite tells you nothing is wrong.

### A payload is a number, and every kind question answered without a tag is a guess waiting to be right

The first draft of the formatting door gave each conversion's argument a payload and no tag. It passed the
integers, the floats and the texts, because for those the payload happens to mean the thing. It failed on
`"%s" % None` (printed nothing at all — `%s` on a NULL char pointer) and on `"%d" % xs[0]` where the slot held
a float (printed `3`). That is ADR 0359's lesson and Gap R.146's, arriving one construct later: the argument
must arrive as the `(payload, tag)` pair the printer reads, and the compile-time gate's only job is to refuse
the arguments whose pair it cannot build. The same class of bug appeared twice more in the same day, both times
as a road that had its own kind question: `isFloat` reading `"%s" % 3.5` as a remainder, and `pairSpecFor`
narrowing away the tag word of a parameter a format reads. Three predicates, one question, one door.

### Textual IR of 1900 lines needs its own verifier, and its own "did the template run" test

Every defect in the first hour of `percent_runtime.go` was an LLVM-level defect discovered by a 40-second
`--file` run: a global named `@rt.pct.argp@`, a message literal whose declared length did not match its bytes,
a label that collided with a parameter (`%cls` vs `cls`), a `br` to a label that introduced an undefined value,
four PHI predecessor mismatches. Two tests removed that feedback loop: the block is verified **standalone**
against `opt -passes=verify` with stub declarations for the twelve runtime helpers it borrows (0.2s), and a
token test fails the build if any `@TAG_…@`/`@CODE_…@` placeholder survives substitution — which is the guard
for the worse failure, a hand-written tag number that verifies cleanly and prints the wrong kind forever.
Messages and tags are generated from `exnClassCode` and `ValueTagList()`, never typed: the two places a number
was spelled by hand were the two that were wrong.

### The seal is the exception semantics, not the message

The door walks the whole format and records the first raise rather than unwinding at it, which is what let
`"%(missing)s %" % {}` report the incomplete conversion and drop the missing key. CPython unwinds, so the first
raise wins. One flag — `@rt.pct.sealed`, checked by every write into the message buffer — turned a whole class
of precedence bugs into one invariant. The lesson generalises past this door: any compiler-side "record the
diagnostic and keep going" design needs to say which record wins, or the last one does, and the last one is
rarely the one the program would have raised.

### `git stash pop` is not a restore, it is a merge

The `git stash list` had three entries from earlier in the loop. Dropping the two newest and popping the third
quietly re-applied a **two-sessions-old** `codegen.go` over the working tree, and a numeric road that had been
rewritten hours earlier came back as if it were current — including a call to a helper that no longer existed,
which is how a "does not compile" error appeared in a file I had already fixed. The tree looked right and was
not. The rule this loop should keep: never pop a stash by index after dropping others; check the entry out to a
file and diff it against the working tree first, and treat any symbol the compiler cannot resolve as a signal
that the file, not the edit, is stale.

### A probe is one program, so it witnesses exactly one refusal

The residue shapes (`"%d" % (2 ** 70)`, `"%s" % (1e100,)`, a nested tuple as an argument, a computed surrogate)
went into one `.gy` probe, and the matrix certified it: `debt`, one note, `compiled leg failed`. Every claim was
true and four claims were unmeasured, because a front-end refusal ends the program before its first line runs —
the second, third and fourth refusals were never reached, and nothing in the harness could tell the difference
between "the program refuses" and "this program refuses in four places". The probe now carries the one line it
can witness and names the rest in its own comment; each sibling got its own program in
`TestPercentArgumentResidueAtTheCLI`, reference answer written into the row. The general rule: a witness
artifact has one verdict, so a family of shapes needs a family of programs — a table of sources, not a program
of statements.

### A doc table is an artifact the day a test parses it

`docs/language.md`'s printf section lists ten answers and fourteen traps as prose tables. The first pass checked
them with a script in `/tmp`, which is the same as not checking them: nothing fails when the door changes and the
doc does not. `TestTheLanguageDocsPercentSectionAnswersWhatItSays` now parses the section out of the file, runs
each documented program through `--aot`, compares the positive rows against CPython too, and floors the row
counts so the section cannot be quietly thinned. It found a formatting subtlety on its first run: the answers are
written after a `#`, and trimming the comment eats the leading spaces that `%5d` deliberately produced, so the
separator must remove exactly one space and keep the rest. A doc claim a test cannot reach is a claim that will
be wrong by the next cycle.

### The golden record is keyed by the source text, so editing a probe orphans its answer

`programs/probe_percent_format.gy` grew the door's conversions, and the GC-corpus case came back with *"no
recorded answer for this corpus program"* — not because the record was deleted, but because the record is keyed
by the exact source, and a rewritten program is a program nobody ever asked. The fix is the ADR 0302 path, not a
delete and not a revert: ask the reference (CPython ran it), cross-check the compiled leg, write the entry, and
then every "N sources" claim in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/operations.md` and `roadmap.md` has to follow the file, because
`golden_artifact_counts_test.go` recomputes them all. Same ratchet, other direction: the door made
`print("a" % 2)` agree with its record, and a **paid** row left on the drift ledger fails the build as loudly as a
new one — so the ledger is rewritten with `GUSTY_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` under the serial `make test`, never under the
concurrent gate, where N processes would each overwrite the ledger with their own subset.

## L11.3 — tuples are values, not syntax sugar (ADR 0361, 2026-10-16)

### A refusal that becomes an answer has to be audited for the wrong answer underneath it

`sorted([(2,1),(1,2)])` refused at the head of this branch, with `unsupported expression *lang.Tuple`. Once
the tuple was an object, the same line printed `[(2, 1), (1, 2)]` — the input, at exit 0. `@rt_sort` compares
payloads (ADR 0339's modes are "number" and "text"), and a container's payload is a **heap slot**: the arrival
order, presented as an order. The refusal had been hiding a fabricated answer that predated tuples (lists did
the same thing), and paying a row had exposed it. Every shape this loop promotes from refusal to answer is
therefore worth asking: *what would the road have printed if it had not stopped?* `TestSortingContainersRefusesRatherThanPrintsArrival`
is that question as a test — three container-element sorts must refuse naming **Gap R.309**, and the two sorts the
door does answer must stay answered, so neither the wrong answer nor a blanket refusal can sneak through.

### The fact belongs on the object; the refusal belongs on the node

The compiled heap has one container layout, so a tuple is that object plus `estrBitTuple` in its own `@estr[h]`
word. Everything that *renders or compares* asks the object — including the roads that only hold a handle at run
time (`rt_tuple_flag` decides `tuple index out of range` from `list index out of range`; the bounds road has no
other witness). Everything that must **stop the build** asks the node, because that is the only moment a build
can be stopped: `t.append(3)` cannot consult an object it has not built yet. Keeping both, and asking each where
it is knowable, is what let one layout serve both spellings without a lie in either direction. The corollary is
that a copy must carry the attributes too — `rt_slice` copying `@estr` is what makes `t[1:]` a tuple — and that a
road whose copy has *no* attribute word (`sorted`, `reversed`, the dict views) must keep its specific printer,
because an object dispatcher that trusts a missing word prints the wrong brackets.

### Re-spelling an AST node is a semantic change in every consumer that pattern-matched on it

Making `(1, 2)` a `*ListLit{Tuple: true}` (rather than a `*Tuple`) was three lines in the parser and a tail of
consumers that had been asking `case *Tuple`: the analyzer's elementwise inference (a variance diagnostic went
silent), the unpack road, and `scalarStoreValue` in `boundflags.go`. That last one was the dangerous one — it
decides whether a name carries a bound flag, and a name whose binding it no longer recognised silently stopped
trapping, so `def f(c): if c: p, q = 1, 2` / `return p` printed `0` where both legs raise `UnboundLocalError`. It
surfaced because an unrelated integration case (`tuple unpack on one branch`) had been written to be sensitive to
exactly that. Two rules came out of it: ask a *predicate* (`g.isTupleExpr`) rather than a node type, and when the
question depends on the binding's shape, pass the shape (`scalarStoreValueForTarget`) instead of inferring it from
the value. The list-shaped twin of each bug was checked every time — if the list road does the same thing, the
behaviour is the shared family (`Gap R.146`, `Gap I.2`) and gets a **parity** test, not an assertion.

### Where the record and the reference disagree, the record keeps its drift row

`print(-("a", 1))` is `TypeError: bad operand type for unary -: 'tuple'` in CPython and the golden record says
`'list'` — the retired engine named the layout it used, and the record copied that. The compiled leg now says
`'tuple'`, which means the row *diverges from the record* and stays on the drift ledger; the harness told me to
delete it as "paid" at the moment the compiled leg still agreed with the record, which is precisely the wrong
direction (ADR 0302: the reference is the definition, the record is evidence and the debt). A row whose shape
changed — `a = (1, 2,)` became buildable, so "cannot build" became "echoed value differs" — is re-recorded with
`GUSTY_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` under the serial `make test`, and the diff is then read line by line: both drift ledgers
had also been re-escaped (`—` → `\u2014`, `>` → `\u003e`) by the writer, and the two files disagree with each
other about escaping, so the diff is normalised back to each file's own HEAD style before the content is judged.

### A record for a promoted probe is asked of the reference, and then the counts move

`probe_tuple.gy` moved from the oracle-debt ledger to an asserted parity program, which made the GC corpus ask a
question nobody had recorded an answer to. `GUSTY_GOLDEN_MISSING` lists it, `tools/recmerge -sources` records it
from CPython and refuses what the compiled leg will not agree to — 7151 → 7152 — and every "N sources" claim in
`AGENTS.md`, `docs/operations.md` and the `roadmap.md` snapshot has to follow the file (Gap R.204 recomputes them).
The historical count inside Gap R.31's own evidence cell (`7119 → 7151`) stays: it describes what that commit did,
not what the file holds now.

### Capability codes for refusals a doc promises, and a suggestion nobody can follow

Two registry entries came with the refusals (`lower.unsupported.tuple-is-immutable`,
`lower.unsupported.sort-elements-have-no-order`), each with a `Sample` that must still refuse or
`TestCLICapabilityRefusalTextRoundTrips` calls the code "a claim about nothing". The first draft of the immutability
suggestion told the user to write `t = t + (3,)` — which this backend also refuses (`Gap R.33`, no list-concatenate),
so the advice would have sent a reader into a second refusal. A suggestion is part of the diagnostic: it may name a
road that exists (`write the literal out`, `build a list for what you mutate`) and must name the missing half rather
than offer a way to run something this toolchain does not run at all.

### Documents are artifacts: run them

The new `docs/language.md` § *Tuples are values* and the README's **Tuples are values** bullet were each extracted
and executed against CPython in the same session (`diff` of compiled stdout against `python3`, empty). Every number
and count claim in them is the file's own. The docs that this row falsified — the dict-key paragraph claiming
`unsupported expression *lang.Tuple`, `d.items()`/`d.popitem()`'s "no tuple value until L11.3", "a tuple is refused
until L11.3 gives it a value to render", the README's stale tuple-in-a-list-of-owed-shapes line — were rewritten to
what the door does now, not softened: a claim a test cannot reach is a claim that will be wrong by the next cycle.

### The three surprises, found by the gate rather than by the plan

**The static global is a trap for a container with an attribute word.** `(1, 2)` of constants wants to fold
to `@.lst1 = global {i32, [N x i32]}`, and that shape has no `@estr[h]` beside it — so a road that handed the
global to `rt_heap_kind` emitted `call i32 @rt_heap_kind(i32 @.lst1)`, `llc` rejected the module, and the run
ended at exit 2, which ADR 0166 reserves for a compiler bug. ADR 0188 had already solved this for lists with
one rule — *the object has to be a heap object because its own bits answer* — and the tuple is the first
container whose answer includes a bit the fold cannot carry. The lesson generalises past tuples: **any new
per-object attribute disqualifies the compile-time global shape**, and the check belongs at the fold door
(`value()`'s list branch, keyed on the literal's own flag), not in each caller.

**A scan that records the wrong kind is worse than a scan that declines.** Routing a tuple-returning
function to the container-return scan's `listAnswer` put it on the list's roads (static answer, road-named
printer → `[1, 2]` for `(1, 2)`, plus the exit-2 above). Removing it from the scan entirely looked cleaner
and was worse: the number door then printed the allocator's word for a container, at exit 0. What was right
is a third answer in the scan — `tupleAnswer` — with the *physical* kind settled as the list's (slots, tag
array, object kind word all say `list`) and the bracket claim recorded separately. When a table has to
describe a value that is physically one thing and presentationally another, add a kind; do not reuse a kind
and do not decline into a fall-through that has a different idea of what the value is.

**Printers that ask the object must be used only where the object owns the answer.** The first cut routed
every list-shaped print through `rt_print_container_value`; three guards noticed immediately, because
`rt_slice` copies the attribute word while `sorted(...)`/`reversed(...)`/the dict views mint objects that
have none — so a slice of a tuple printed right and a sorted list printed an interned index. The rule that
came out: the dispatcher reads an attribute word, so only roads whose object *carries* one may ask it; roads
whose object has no attribute word keep their specific printer. A reuse that "works on my program" is a
claim about the door's precondition, and the precondition belongs in the commit message and the comment.

**Process: a feature that lands turns refusal-guards into liabilities, fast.** Eight tests in this cycle
failed not because the codegen was wrong but because they were written to fail the day the answer arrived
("this compiles — the roadmap row says it is not answered"). That is the design working: each carried the
roadmap row in its message, and the honest move each time was to move the case into the answered table and
say, in the comment, which shape of the row is still owed (Gap R.295's tuple element, Gap R.302's mixed and
nested patterns, Gap R.212's list key). What must never happen is deleting the case or softening the
sentence; and what must also not happen is keeping a refusal the language no longer needs —
`lower.unsupported.tuple-value` left the capability registry for exactly that reason.

## L11.5 — a text is a sequence of code points, and one generated table decides its case (ADR 0362, 2026-10-16)

**A hand-written expectation is not a witness.** The first version of the trim table pinned
`"  ΑΣ  ".lstrip()` as `"ΑΣ"` and `"  x a  ".strip(" xa")` as `"a"`, and both guards were green — because they
compared the compiler against my guess about the compiler. Measured against `python3` inside the same case, the
reference answers `"ΑΣ  "` and `""`: `strip` removes what the reference calls whitespace and nothing else, and a
cutset is a set of *characters*, not a prefix to peel. The rule that came out of being wrong twice: a row that
states an answer must ask the reference for that answer **in the same test**, and fail on the row's own
disagreement — `TestTheCaseEngineAnswersTheReferencesSpecialCasings` and its trim twin do exactly that, and each
one failed on my rows before it failed on the compiler's. A hand-typed `want` is a claim about a language, and
the language is defined elsewhere.

**A road that produces a value must be registered with the predicates that classify values.** Three separate
silent failures came from the same omission. `print(f("  café "))` printed `1`, the intern index, because
`isStrUnder` knew `.strip` was not a text-returning method (and a *second* copy of that list, `argcOf`, kept the
old zero-argument shape of `strip`, so the two halves disagreed about the same call). `len(w.upper())` stopped the
build with `len requires an inline list/dict/set literal` where the reference answers `2` for `w = "ß"`, because the
`len` road
enumerated the *shapes* it could measure and a method call was not one of them. `f(xs[0])` and `f(g())` — the same
text arriving from a container slot or a call — were refused as `len of a non-string variable`, and the refusal
said *variable*, describing a program the author had not written. The fix was not three patches but one rule,
ADR 0229's: every consumer asks one predicate — *does this expression answer text?* — and the predicate knows the
case doors, the trim doors, a call whose every return answers text, an element of a literal container whose
elements are all text, and a slice or index of a text. Where the measurement could not reach, the door was still
asked for the right one: the `len` road measured an interned text with `rt_str_len`, the byte counter, while the
code-point counter `rt_str_nchars` sits beside it in the same block, and the two `len` arms now ask the character
door — a switch no program of mine distinguished (every road that reaches the object asks the object, which
already answers in characters), and the entry says so rather than inventing a wrong answer to justify it. When a
new value-producing road lands, the classification pass is part of it; otherwise the new road prints the word it
stores rather than the value it holds, at exit 0.

**A self-edge in a fixpoint is not a cycle.** The call-argument classifier decided too much:
`def f(s): x = s[1:3]; return x` printed `1` because the scan that folds a parameter's text from the call site
gave up on `x` — its right-hand side mentioned `x`. Dropping every fact for a name that mentions itself is the
easy rule and the wrong one: a fixpoint tolerates a self-edge by comparing against the previous round instead of
removing the node. The self-referential arm is now skipped while the rest of the body's bindings are recorded,
and `s = "x"; x = s[1:3]` keeps the text it was declared to hold. Two lessons in one line: fixpoints keep stale
values rather than no values, and a heuristic that "conservatively declines" must say *what* it declines — the
sentence that came out named the mixed container element it refused to classify, which is what told me the
remaining refusal was honest rather than accidental.

**Probe the reference's behaviour, never its labels.** The generated artifact asks CPython four questions per
code point: the four case mappings where they differ from identity, `("1" + c + "a").title()` for *cased*, both
sigma looks around `ΑΣ` for *case-ignorable*, and `c.strip() == ""` for *whitespace*. Each is a behaviour rather
than a category, and the difference is not academic: the Unicode category of U+0345 makes it cased and
case-ignorable at once, which is why `"ͅΣ".lower()` answers `ͅσ` and a category-driven engine answers `ͅς`; and
`unicode.IsSpace` does not count U+001C as whitespace while `str.strip` does. A table copied from a data file, or
from Go's `strings.ToUpper`/`unicode.IsSpace`, is a claim about what Unicode says; a table probed from the
reference is a claim about what *this language* answers. The 29-entry whitespace set, the 4526-entry cased set and
the 2707-entry ignorable set all came out of the reference, and `casetab -check` re-asks the reference rather than
re-checking a committed number.

**Measure the "before" with the old binary, or write the wrong history.** The ADR's first measured table said the
compiled leg *refused* `"ǅ".title()` and printed `İ` for `"İ".lower()`. Measuring against the pre-change binary
(`/tmp/gzhead`) says otherwise: the fold answered `Ǆ` and `i` — wrong answers at exit 0 — and it was the *runtime*
door (a text the compiler cannot read) that refused `title` and `swapcase`. Those are different defects with
different lessons, and the difference is only visible if the comparison is run rather than remembered. Every row
of that table is now a test (`TestTheAdrsMeasuredRowsAnswerTheReference`, compiled output compared with CPython in
the same case), so the ADR's history and the compiler's present cannot drift apart.

**Process: a feature that lands is a snapshot-count event.** One commit touched five artifacts and therefore four
guards: the record grew 7152 → 7606 (454 sources, every one written by `tools/recmerge` from CPython's answer with
the compiled leg cross-checked), the conformance programs 213 → 214, the matrix 200 → 201, the oracle's `match`
column 154 → 155, the ADRs 352 → 353, and the queue's rows-owed 158 → 156. Each guard named the file and the
position of the stale number, which is Gap R.204 doing its job — and the discipline is to edit the *cell* after
re-running the measurement, never to edit the measurement to suit the cell. The same rule caught me writing
"1400 code points" in a comment for a table that holds 1112064: a number in prose is a bug waiting to be believed,
so it either comes from the artifact or it is not written at all.

## Round 10 — the key door writes the call the AST never wrote (ADR 0363, Gap R.264, 2026-10-17)

**The row's own diagnosis was half wrong, and the control experiment said so before any code.** `roadmap.md`
said `sorted(['bbb','a','cc'], key=lambda s: len(s))` refused because the key's parameter arrives as one
untagged word, so `len` of a variable has no kind to ask. The control is one keystroke away:
`def k(s): return len(s)` / `print(k("abc"))` prints `3`, and the same `k` as `key=k` refuses. Same parameter,
same body, same untagged word — the difference is only *who calls it*. So the tag was never the missing fact;
the missing fact was that `strArgKinds`, the scan that decides which parameters receive texts, reads call sites
**out of the AST**, and the door's call is not in the AST — `keyCallReg` synthesises `key(element)` at lowering
time. Lesson: when a row hands you a cause, run the pair that differs by one thing and see whether the cause it
names is the difference you measure. Half of this cycle would have been spent teaching a door to trust an
unproven variable, which is ADR 0166's worst class wearing a fix.

**A refusal can be the map to a wrong answer two files away.** While wiring the key's parameter I probed the
bound form too — `xs = sorted(["bbb","a"])` then `print(xs, xs[0])` — and got `['a', 'bbb'] 1` at **exit 0**,
the intern table's numbering where the reference prints `a`. That bug predated this row and had nothing to do
with a lambda: the assignment arm that settles what a bound container holds asked `call.Args[0]` only when it
was a `*Name` (`g.listElemStr[src]`), and beside a key the argument is the literal the door copies itself. One
reading, `keyDoorOptions`, now serves both askers (ADR 0232): `keyDoorCallSites` hands the parameter scan the
candidates the key will be called with, `keyDoorCandidates` hands the variable census the same candidates plus
the distinction the builtins draw — `sorted` answers a *container* of them, `min`/`max` answer *one* of them —
which is why `best = max(words, key=len)` binds a text and `best.upper()` answers, while
`xs = sorted(words, key=len)` binds a list of texts and prints, indexes and walks as one. A door that builds a
container has to register its element kind where the bindings are settled, or the print road renders a payload
the reference renders as a value.

**Claims, never guesses.** `strArgClaimOf` is now the single predicate under the ordinary call site and the
door, so ADR 0348's cancellation still fires: `def k(s): return len(s)` called with `3` and used as a text key
cancels to unclaimed and refuses, which is `TestTheKeyDoorsCallSitesAreReadByTheParameterScan`'s
"contradictory evidence" row. `allElemsPrintAsText` is written the same way — one non-text element and the
answer is *no*, which leaves the container on the mixed printer that can render every kind. A census that
guesses is a census that prints an index at exit 0.

**A guard that reads a counter written by parallel children cannot see the work.** Both record-leg guards —
"the answer table matches no record row at all" / "not one of this row's programs is on the record" — failed on
a run where every record was walked, because `t.Parallel()` subtests do not run until *after* the parent's
function body returns, and `asked++` lives in the parent. The failure looked like missing records; the records
were there (the file had 7636 entries and `HasGoldenAnswer` said so in a scratch test). Any parent-level
"did the leg run at all" assertion must drop `t.Parallel()` on its children — and the counter pattern is worth
checking in the tests I write from now on, because it fails *closed*, which is the direction that wastes an
hour.

**The record is written by the reference or not at all, and the count guards then collect the toll.** 30 new
sources went in through `tools/recmerge`, which asks CPython and cross-checks the LLVM JIT and refuses an entry
the two legs disagree on: 7606 → 7636. Four sentences then had to be recomputed from the file — the artifact
table in `docs/operations.md`, the record-leg sentence in `AGENTS.md`, and two cells of `roadmap.md`'s Snapshot
— and each guard named the file, the position and both numbers. That is Gap R.204 being paid on schedule rather
than discovered late, and it is the cheapest possible reviewer: I did not decide those numbers, I read them off
failures.

**Read the module before asserting on it.** My IR-shape case asserted `call i32 @rt_str_order(` for
`sorted(["z","a","Mb"], key=lambda s: s.lower())` and failed on a *correct* build: the keyed door orders texts
with `call i32 @rt_elem_gt(i32 %a, i32 %b, i32 1)`, whose mode-1 arm does the `strcmp` inside the comparator,
and `rt_str_order` belongs to the unkeyed `min`/`max` fold. The assertion was written from memory of the
runtime's vocabulary instead of from the module in front of me; dumping the emitted IR fixed it in one step. The
same discipline — build the pre-change binary (`/tmp/probe/gustyc_base`) beside the new one and diff answer for
answer — is what proved the float and `reversed` wrongness in the neighbourhood (Gap R.248, Gap R.251) was
already there and is not this commit's, which keeps one commit to one feature.

## Round 11 — a clone answers the recursion in its own body by calling itself (ADR 0364, Gap R.267, Gap R.313, 2026-10-18)

**The most ordinary program in the language was refused, and the suite could not have seen it.** `def fact(n,
f): … return f(n) * fact(n - 1, f)` / `print(fact(4, lambda x: x))` — CPython's `24` — exited 1 here with
`"f" is called but is not a function this backend can build a call to`, the same sentence for eight shapes.
ADR 0345's pass clones a higher-order body once per tuple of functions its call sites hand its parameters, and
every program the suite contains has the recursion *removed*: `twice(fn, v)`, `apply1(fn, v)`, `key=lambda`.
A feature that ships with a table of answered shapes also ships the shape nobody thought to write down; the
missing row was not "higher-order functions" but "higher-order functions **that recurse**".

**One missing coordinate, not one missing feature.** The plan builds entry tuples out of *call sites*, and a
call written inside a higher-order body is not a call site — it is the body's own call. With no site the
recursion's callable slot had no entry, the plan declined, `applyDefunctionalization` returned the tree
untouched (correctly: all-or-nothing is what lets the pass run before the front end's own tools), and codegen
met `f(n)` in an un-specialised body. The refusal therefore named the *parameter* for a decision a pass had
made one stage earlier. ADR 0166 was being obeyed and still produced a diagnostic that pointed at the wrong
thing — "the door that refuses must name the missing half" needs a second clause: *the door must be the one
that knows*.

**A rule can be right and still be the bug.** ADR 0345's eligibility rule — a called parameter that is also
*read* is not substitutable — is what keeps `print(f)` refused. It also made `fact(n - 1, f)` ineligible,
because the recursion mentions `f` in an argument position. The pass declined its own feature's canonical
program because of the syntax that makes it that program. The carve-out had to be exact: not "a parameter may
appear in the recursion" (which would let `run(n - 1, f + 1)` through), but "the argument at position i *is*
the parameter i, by node identity" — `callableSelfPassThrough` returns the nodes, and only those nodes stop
counting as reads. `xs = [f]`, `print(f)`, `return f` still make the function unrewritten, and the invariant
`callableNoFunctionValuesLeft` is where that is actually verified — on the tree that was produced, with the
bodies the pass marked `SkipEmit` excluded, because those bodies are gone rather than hiding.

**Two fields for two questions, or a guard that verifies the wrong thing.** `def run(v, fn): return fn(v)`
refused too, and it has no recursion at all: a call of a parameter records *which parameter it evaluates*
(`pos`) and *which entry of the clone's tuple that parameter is* (`slot`, the order the called parameters were
collected). The rewrite read `pos` as the tuple index. They agree whenever the callable comes first, which is
how every program in this suite is written — the bug's precondition occurred thousands of times in the corpus
and its failure never once. Worse, the audit beside it (`callableInnerAgrees`, "are the entries declared for
the calls the body makes?") asked its correct, complete question of the wrong field. A guard that checks the
wrong field is the same failure as no guard, and quieter. Filed as its own row (**Gap R.313**) rather than
folded into the feature that found it, because a fixed coordinate needs a test that would have failed before.

**Once the pass owns a shape, it owns its refusals.** Four recursions have no answer, and leaving them to
codegen meant one sentence standing for four programs. Each now has its own: the recursion hands the callable
to something else (`run(n - 1, other)` — the clone would need an entry for `other` too, chosen mid-recursion);
it omits a parameter; it is written inside a `lambda` (whose hoisted body has a declaration and no frame); two
higher-order bodies recurse into each other. The mutual case had to be declined at the one place the pass
knows nothing else was rewritable — a decline that fires on a program with work to do would take an answer away
from an unrelated higher-order call, which is ADR 0273's rule wearing a different hat.

**No value word was needed, and saying so is half the ADR.** The temptation was to give the callable a tag (a
`fnptr`, a symbol index) so the recursion could carry it. That is L11.1's row — what R.266/R.268/R.281 wait on
— and this row does not need it: the recursion hands the parameter *the function it already arrived with*, so
the entry is the one the clone was minted for. The result is `call i32 @gy_fact$callable$…(i32 %t9, i32 0)` — a
call to a `define` whose name the pass wrote, no `ptrtoint`, no indirect `call`, nothing added to the runtime.
Two rejections worth keeping: a second clone per recursion-tuple (the same fixed point as a bigger table,
multiplying definitions for a coordinate that cannot vary), and following the recursion to a fixed point
(which would have to *guess* what the recursion's callable will be, and guess wrong on exactly the program the
decline now names).

**The machine path grew one number that pays for itself.** `recursive_sites` in `--callables` says how many
calls written inside a higher-order body now name that body's own clone. It is not decoration: a clone that
recursed through the un-specialised entry — the bug class this row is about — cannot leave the field at a
plausible value by accident. Schema (`definitions.callablePassReport`), `docs/operations.md`, the agentic
doc and `gustyc --lang`'s `callable values:` line all moved with it, and the agentic example is a real document
printed by the tool for a source printed beside it.

**Test-writing lessons, each bought with a red run.**
- *Compare decoded JSON, not bytes.* Three assertions failed on a correct build because the account is JSON and
  a sentence inside it arrives as `hands \"f\" something`: `strings.Contains(doc, "hands \"f\" something")` is
  false. Unmarshal into the report struct and compare the decoded field; a refusal the pass names exactly reads
  as a pass that said nothing.
- *Assert on the module you dumped, not the module you remember.* My IR rows wanted `call … @gy_module$lambda$…(i32
  %t\d+)`; the clone calls the entry with its own parameter register (`%p0`). One dump settled both rows.
- *A negative table must state which mouth speaks.* Two rows in the refusal table were front-end refusals
  (`expects 2 arguments`) whose citation contract differs from a codegen refusal's; the "must point at a row"
  assertion needed a flag rather than a fudge.
- *Don't record a program no leg answers.* `tools/recmerge` stops at the first disagreement, which is right, and
  made me build the answered/refused split myself first: 56 candidate sources → 50 records, the 6 dropped being
  exactly the refusal rows. The corpus program's text recursion needs a base case that returns `""`, not `0` —
  a mixed return type across arms is a *different* row, and pinning it here would have made a red test out of a
  neighbour's work.
- *The parent-counter trap again:* the two "did the leg run at all" guards need children without `t.Parallel()`;
  I wrote them that way from the start this time and they passed the first run.

## Gap R.33 — the sequence door (ADR 0365), 2026-07-29

- **The defect was a position, not a missing helper.** `[1] + [2]` emitted `add i32 @.lst1, @.lst2` because
  by the time `+` looked, the operand was an `i32` that used to be a list. Every road that wants to know an
  operand's kind has to ask while it is still an `Expr`; the fix is the door's placement, and the helpers are
  the easy half. The same lesson ADR 0360 recorded for `%` one operator over.
- **Payload and tag travel together, including when you are the one making the object.** The two copies walk
  payload and tag slot for slot; a list built with payloads only would print, compare and index as a number
  wearing another object's bits, which is ADR 0187's failure mode arriving from the other direction.
- **A text is an index, so `rt_str_repeat` interns.** The first version returned a pointer; `len("ab" * 3)`
  answered 5 and an f-string field printed a digit. Every text road in this codebase is a `(index, length)`
  pair, and ADR 0222 forbids the conversion nobody wrote (Gap R.42 again).
- **A refusal must be true of the compiler that prints it.** The old refusal said "the backend builds no
  runtime list-concatenate, sequence-repeat or container-ordering helper". Once it built two of the three,
  that sentence was a lie in an agent's face — so the mixed pairs (`[1] + (1, 2)`, `{1} + {2}`) moved to
  raises and the three remaining refusals name the missing arm plus Gap R.314.
- **Two predicates that can disagree about a value are one bug waiting to be filed.** The printer, `str()`,
  `repr()`, an f-string field, `==`, `in` and the loop all ask the same `seqHandleOf`/`seqBuildsContainer`
  pair, the way ADR 0232 made the container roads ask one door. Writing a fourth `isBuiltSeq` is how the
  next cycle loses an hour.
- **Process:** the drift ledger is a paid-debt alarm, not a log — four rows came off it in this cycle, and
  the run told me each one by source. `tools/recmerge -sources <file>` is the only honest way to add golden
  entries (52 across the cycle; the counts guard is a hash over the array, so the tool has to write it). And the
  gate is `make testparallel`; a serial `go test ./...` on this suite is a 40-minute read.
- **A widening exposes the roads that were never registered.** Unifying the formatting and the repeat under
  one text predicate (`textDoorIsText`) made the method road print **two** wrong lines where it had printed
  one — `return "x%s" % s` and `return s * 2` in a method that takes a parameter both print the `@str_tab`
  index. That is Gap R.315, filed in the same commit as the door, recorded as
  `integration/programs/probe_method_text_answer.gy` with the reference's five lines beside this backend's
  five. The lesson is the opposite of hiding it: one predicate makes a half-registered road measurable, and
  two predicates let the two doors disagree in private for three cycles.
- **A program that becomes an answer is promoted, not edited.** `programs/sequence_ops.gy` stayed a probe —
  it also asks for the order of two containers — and the shapes this door does answer went into a new parity
  program, `programs/sequence_builds.gy`. Promoting the old one would have quietly dropped the ordering line
  and un-pinned Gap R.314; a corpus row's job is to keep measuring the thing it was written to measure.
- **Counts move under you.** Adding a program and a probe moved four Snapshot rows (programs, matrix rows,
  divergences, `debt` verdicts) plus the owed-queue tally, and `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered`
  named each one rather than letting me type a guess. Re-run it after the artifact-writing runs, not before.

## ADR 0366 — a method is a callable, so its parameter and its answer carry their kind (2026-10-16)

- **A census keyed by a name is a census about `def`s until it reads methods.** Four programs, one root:
  `def fmt(self, s): return "x%s" % s` printed `x0`, `def rep(self, s): return s * 2` printed `0`, `def yes(self):
  return 1 == 1` printed `1`, and `def upper(self, s): return s.upper()` died by SIGSEGV. Each had a function twin
  that was already right, and that pairing is the whole diagnosis — the print road asked `bodyReturnsOnlyBools` of
  a `*Name` callee and never of an `*Attr` one, and the text census claimed args from `f(x)` and never from
  `obj.m(x)`. The fix is one predicate per question, asked of both spellings; a method-side twin of a predicate is
  how the two roads drift apart (ADR 0299 again, in a new costume).
- **`internedVars` is authoritative, not additive.** Registering a method's classified parameter had to *delete*
  the claim when the census withholds it, exactly as `funcDef` does; an additive write left a previous body's
  claim on the same name and printed a text where the body reads a number.
- **The census's own call sites can poison it.** `class C: def upper(self, s): return s.upper()` reported the
  body's `s.upper()` — a zero-argument call by the walker's reading — as a call that "left position 1 to its
  default", and the evidence-against rule unmarked the parameter the real call site had just marked. The bound had
  to become narrower than the rule that looked natural: only a tail position with a real `Default` is evidence
  against. A tail the signature requires is a program CPython rejects, not a kind the compiler distrusts.
- **The receiver's kind picks the method table.** `callMethod` is a sequence of roads keyed by the *method name*;
  the class table and the text-method table share those names, so `s.upper()` resolved to the enclosing class and
  recursed until the address space ran out. Asking `exprIsString` before the class and dynamic-dispatch roads —
  and keeping the class road for a receiver whose class is known — turned the artifact fault into `HI`. A text is
  never an instance: skipping a road that could only be wrong for it can never lose an answer.
- **`, _ :=` on a road that emits IR is an exit 2 waiting to happen.** `h, _ := g.value(b, attr.Obj)` produced
  `rt_mkobj(i32 10, i32 )` and `llc` rejected the module, while the sentence the program deserved lived two lines
  away in the neighbouring road. Propagating the operand's error is the difference between a compiler bug and a
  refusal; grep your own package for `, _ := g.value(` before the next cycle does it for you (Gap R.318).
- **A defaulted parameter is a slot nothing wrote.** The moment the census interned a method's text default, the
  program SIGSEGVed: the dispatch passes only the arguments the source wrote, so interning a default is the
  callee's prologue's job, not the call site's. Withholding the claim is the honest interim (Gap R.320), and the
  refusal rows are pinned so a future cycle has to move the row rather than delete it.
- **Fields need the "every write, or no claim" rule.** `return self.flag` is a verdict because every write of
  `flag` in the program hands one; one `obj.flag = 3` anywhere retires the name for every class, because the
  compiler cannot tell which object a write reached. The text twin of that reading is **Gap R.319**, pinned with
  today's `0`/`1` beside CPython's `hi`/`yo` — a wrong value at exit 0 is filed, never asserted as an answer.
- **Promotions are earned twice.** `probe_method_text_answer.gy` and `probe_method_verdict_answer.gy` and
  `probe_method_shadows_text_method.gy` moved from `debt` to `match` only after `tools/recmerge` agreed to write
  their entries — the recorder refuses a source whose compiled leg disagrees with the reference, which is the
  check that makes the promotion a claim rather than an edit (`checked 3, added 2, entries 7741`).
- **Process:** three conformance failures told me exactly which rows had stopped being debt; the matrix artifact
  rewrote itself under `TestConformanceMatrix`; `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered` named each stale
  count (programs 219→220, rows 206→207, parity 172→174, `debt` 26→25, record 7739→7741) instead of letting me
  type a guess. And a temporary `zz_debug_test.go` in `pkg/lang` is fine only while you remember to delete it —
  the package's guards treat a stray test file as part of the language's evidence.

## ADR 0368 — a call that answers more than one kind carries its kind beside its payload (Gap R.219, Gap R.228, 2026-10-17)

- **A table keyed by a name is a claim about ONE payload.** `strFuncs` registered a function as
  text-returning when *any* return yielded text, and the call site then rendered every answer with
  `rt_print_str`. The bug was not the printer and not the call road: it was that the module recorded one
  fact per function where the program had one fact per `return`. `pkg/lang/answer_kind.go` moves the
  record from the name to the road, which is the whole fix; everything else in the commit is the four
  readers learning to ask.
- **The measurement had to be against the parent commit, not against memory.** The first version of the
  ADR claimed "18 of 25 shapes changed answer". Rebuilding HEAD in a worktree (`git worktree add
  --detach /tmp/head-wt HEAD`, then `go build -o /tmp/gustyc-head ./cmd/gustyc`) and running one probe
  script over both binaries said **12 changed, 13 were already right, 7 remain**. The number in the
  tracker is the measured one; a claim about a change that was never compared to the before-state is a
  story, and this repo's guards exist precisely because stories drift. Two of the 7 are pre-existing
  (Gap R.83's comparison, the pair road's own refusal) and stayed on their own rows rather than being
  adopted to make the story tidier.
- **The exit-2 face of a wrong answer is easy to miss.** `def f(x): if x: return "a"` / `    return [1, 2]`
  did not print the wrong thing — it lowered `ret i32 @.lst1` and `llc` rejected the module. Measuring
  "which answers differ from CPython" alone found it only because the probe recorded *how* each shape
  failed. A shape that dies at exit 2 is a different severity from a shape that prints `0`, and ADR 0166's
  ban makes it a defect even when nobody filed it.
- **A gate that fires where nobody reads the fact is a trap, not a gate.** The first attempt seeded the
  pair road's `pairRetDone` from the new plan, which is the obvious reuse — same global, same pair. It
  turned `while f():` of a mixed body into an exit-1 refusal: ADR 0273's rule, met by a compiler that had
  just been improved. The answer road is now an **opt-in**: the doors that read a tag (`print`,
  `str`/`repr`, a truth test, an f-string field, a container element, an expression statement) ask
  `answerCallPair`; the doors that keep one word carry `!g.answer.carries(name)` and answer as they always
  did. Those five shapes are Gap R.324 with the reference's answer pinned beside the compiled one in
  `TestWhatTheAnswerDirectionStillCannotReachIsFiledNotFixed`, which fails on either side — if a door
  opens, its row has to be deleted before the suite goes green.
- **Declining is a feature of the gate.** The scan names a kind only when the source spells it. A body
  whose arm returns a *name*, a float, an attribute or an `if`-expression is left exactly where it was.
  That is why `return 1.5` / `return 2` still prints `2.0` and `return "a"` / `return 1.5` still refuses:
  a guess about a payload is the defect this cycle exists to remove, and re-introducing one in the gate
  that removes the others would be worse than the debt.
- **Write the plan as a value, not a global (ADR 0343, again).** `pairCallScan` learned this the hard way;
  the answer scan is built by `answerKindPlanOf` and *returned*, so two compiles in flight cannot be
  answered by one plan. `TestAnswerKindPlanIsNotAPackageVariable` is the cheap guard that keeps it true.
- **A fixed point needs rounds.** `return other(...)` is answerable only once `other` is, and `other`'s
  verdict may depend on a third body. One pass over the source answers `false` for a body written above
  its callee and `true` for the same body written below it. Marking grows monotonically, so six rounds
  settle; the test writes the program both ways and demands one answer.
- **Guards over the tracker are guards over the truth.** Three of them bit during this cycle and all
  three were right: `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered` refused "ADRs 358" once
  `docs/adr/0368-*.md` existed, and refused "158 of 229 queue rows" once two rows closed and one opened;
  `TestTheRoadmapsCitationsResolve` reads every file and `::Test…` an Evidence cell cites; and
  `queuePri`'s `^[0-9]+[a-z]?$` rejected a `26ab` priority outright — a row whose Pri column does not
  match stops the queue tally dead in its tracks, silently hiding every row below it (46 counted instead
  of 229). **A new queue row needs a single-letter suffix.**
- **Verify a belief about the code before you reason from it.** Half-way through I was reasoning about
  `pairCallSiteClaims`, `fnReturnsFloat` and `emitPrintln` — three functions that do not exist in this
  repository. `grep` cost seconds each; the reasoning they were supporting was worth none of the time it
  would have taken to "fix" them. Every claim in the ADR's consequences table is a line of measured output
  from `/tmp/matrix/run.sh`, not a deduction from a function name I expected to find.

## ADR 0369 — a hook reads its key from the name a lambda was bound to (Gap R.281, Gap R.325, 2026-10-18)

- **A position the compiler calls is a position the compiler must tell itself about.** `sorted(xs, key=neg)`
  with `neg = lambda v: 0 - v` died with `TypeError: 'int' object is not callable` because the defunctionalisation
  pass rewrites *calls*, and a `key=` is not one — the door emits it. The AST shows an expression; the semantics
  contain a call. Every soundness argument in `pkg/lang/callable_value.go` is "this name is only ever a callee,
  tested by node identity", and node identity cannot see a callee that lives in an option. The fix is not a new
  mechanism: it is `keyDoorOptions`, the reader the door and ADR 0363's census already share, plus a set that says
  *a name here is being called*. Three readers of one construct would have been the real bug.
- **The two controls were the whole diagnosis, and they were already in the tracker.** Gap R.281's cell recorded
  that the inline hook answers and the `def` hook answers. Once I trusted that, the space of causes collapsed to
  "the name", and the row was an argument-position retarget rather than a new callable representation. A gap row
  that records its controls is worth more than a gap row that records its symptom; the symptom alone would have
  pointed at the door.
- **Measure the before-binary again, even for a row you think you understand.** `gustyc_base` (HEAD~0 built from
  a stash) showed that five shapes I had just "broken" or "fixed" were identical before and after: `print(neg)`
  answering `undefined name`, a callable reaching a user-defined hook's parameter, and a body returning a folded
  container printing `0` or dying at exit 2. Those are not this row's regressions — they are three new rows
  (Gaps R.326, R.327, R.328) filed instead of quietly absorbed, and one of them (`ret i32 @.lst1`) is an exit-2
  compiler bug on a program with no function value in it. Without the before-binary I would have "fixed" two of
  them in this commit and missed the third entirely.
- **A diagnostic that prints a generated symbol is a bug with an existing helper for it.** After the retarget the
  AST holds `neg$lambda$a78954b_0`, and the key door builds its messages from that AST, so the arity trap said
  `neg$lambda$a78954b_0() takes 0 positional arguments…` where CPython says `<lambda>()…`. `callableSurfaceName`
  already solved this for the call road; the door was simply not calling it. The lesson is the one ADR 0166 keeps
  teaching: minting a name is a promise that the name stays private, and every new surface that reads the
  rewritten tree is a place that promise can break. Gap R.325 is filed for the leak's pre-existing half and paid
  beside the row that made it reachable from a binding.
- **Count the rewrite into the hash.** `key_arguments` went into the report and into `callablePlanHash` in the same
  edit, because the second is the guard for the first: two programs differing only in a hook the pass answered
  would otherwise share a digest, and every lit-style row that reads that digest would certify one rewrite for
  two. The test (`TestTheNamedHookAccountCountsItsKeys`) adds a second hook and fails if the hash stands still.
- **The withdrawal is correct even when the sentence after it is wrong.** `print(neg)` shows the pass doing its job
  — `rewritten: false`, `refused: ["the rewrite was withdrawn: …used a function as a value"]` — and the *emitter*
  then deleting the binding so the read becomes `undefined name`. A guard that only reads the pass's account would
  pass. Read the whole program's outcome, not the component's verdict.
- **Record leg, reference leg, and the recorder's own mode.** `tools/recmerge -check` asserts a source is *not*
  answerable (the mode for refusals); writing new answers is the default mode. The record went 7762 → 7785, every
  entry written from CPython with the compiled leg cross-checked, and the corpus program that had been written
  *around* this gap (`lambda_default_param.gy`, whose header said so) grew its named-hook rows back.

## ADR 0370 — an applied `lambda` is a function this backend can build a call to (L11.7, Gap R.265, Gap R.276, 2026-10-19)

- **Key the clone on the caller, not on the callee.** `(lambda f: f(1) + f(2))(lambda x: x * 3)` and
  `(lambda f: f(3))(lambda x: x * 2)` apply *the same written lambda* at two different argument tuples. My first cut
  registered the higher-order body under the inner `Lambda` node, so the second application was pointed at the clone
  built for the first and answered `6` for a program whose answer is `9` — a wrong value at exit 0, on a shape the row
  had just been declared paid. The key is the **call node**: an entry belongs to an application, and the argument tuple
  an entry means is the one that application writes.
- **A `lambda` is a declaration; ask the binding rule, not the frame's table.** Deriving a lambda's captures from
  `closureInfoFor` — the nested-`def` road's filter over names the enclosing frame has a slot for — deleted `x` from
  `(lambda x: (lambda y: (lambda z: x + y + z)(100))(10))(1)`'s two-frame twin, because `x` is bound by a lambda and
  not by a frame table. `lambdaFreeNames` (with `scanFreeIn`/`scanCompScope`/`childScope` for the scopes a body opens)
  is the question the language asks; the table is one road's answer to it.
- **Ask the call sites, not just the body.** `def f(v): return (lambda k: k + v)(1)` applied as `f(2.5)` is invisible
  to the body's float tables: inside the body `v` is a parameter of nobody. `captureParamWord` therefore scans
  `callableCallsOf` for every call of the frame — including the clone ownership `g.lambdaOrigin[fd] == fn` and the
  parameter's own `Default` — and types the capture from what the program actually hands in. The alternative was a
  truncated number at exit 0.
- **A gate is worth nothing if it is asked after the thing it gates.** The capture-word check has to run **before**
  `emitLambdaBody`, because emitting the body is what commits the module to an `i32` per capture. Asked afterwards it
  could only report on a module it had already built, and the only honest thing left to do with that module was to
  throw it away — which is exactly when a wrong value escapes into the `printf` that was emitted for it.
- **`g.params` is the only trustworthy "is this a parameter?".** `paramSlot` is empty for a parameter the body never
  rebinds, so `isParam` was false for exactly the captures that matter — a body reads `x` and never writes it. The
  symptom was a captured parameter answering `0` at exit 0. Ask the map, not the slot map.
- **Two roads streaming their own `define` into `g.globals` at once is a collision waiting to happen.** A lambda
  emitted inside a method or a closure body landed in the middle of the enclosing `define` and `llc` answered
  `multiple definition of local value named 'gc.frame.base'`. The fix is a third stream — `g.lambdaDefines`, written
  after `g.strGlobals` in `GenerateIR` — plus `g.curFD`, because `g.curFunc` is set only by the `funcDef` road and the
  closure and method roads bypass it (they now save/restore `inFunc`/`curFD`/`emittingMethod`, and `emitClosureDef`
  gives its body its **own** `%<name>.raiseexit` label before restoring the enclosing one).
- **When a neighbour's road answers one word, refuse rather than emit a module `llc` rejects.** A float-answering
  lambda applied inside a closure or a method has no word to travel back in; the temptation was to emit the `double`
  call and let the verifier be the problem. `lambdaFrameAnswersDoubles` refuses at exit 1 instead, because ADR 0166
  makes an exit 2 a compiler bug on a program the reference runs — and the module really was rejected: that is how
  `print((lambda m: m / 2)(3))` presented itself before `isFloat`/`floatValue` learned that a call of a `Lambda` can
  answer a float (`call double @gy_lambda_0` printed through a `%d`).
- **The record cannot be widened by the thing under test.** All 39 new sources were written by `tools/recmerge`, which
  asks CPython and cross-checks the compiled leg, and it refuses to record a source whose compiled leg refuses or
  disagrees. Three of my table rows turned out to be *refusals* I had mistaken for answers (`(lambda f: y=…)` with the
  default omitted, `(lambda f: f(3))(abs)`, a capture three frames up) — `recmerge` caught all three by refusing to
  write them, which is the soundness property doing its job as a test-time oracle.
- **A wrong answer that predates the commit is still a wrong answer, and belongs in a row.** Module-level
  `t = "hey"` above `print((lambda: t)())` prints `0` at exit 0 — and printed `0` on the stash-built before-binary
  too. It is not this row's regression, so it is **Gap R.331**, filed with the reference's answer beside it and the
  record rows carrying `hey`, rather than being absorbed into this commit or dropped from the table.
- **A filed table's own rule is delete, not edit.** `TestWhatTheLambdaDefaultRowLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed` pinned
  two `Gap R.276` refusals with the instruction "close it and delete this case"; both cases went in the same commit as
  the fix, and what remains in that table is what is still refused (the value-word wall, **Gap R.332**). A guard that
  quietly keeps asserting a fixed shape is a test that has stopped testing.
- **The tracker's counts are guards, not notes.** `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered`,
  `TestTheArtifactTableCountsAreTheFilesOwn` and `TestTheRecordedSourceCountInTheAgentFacingDocsIsTheFilesOwn` failed
  the moment the record grew (7785 → 7827) and the ADR count moved (360 → 361, highest `0370`); each names the file
  whose number is the truth, and editing the sentence is the fix — the test is not to be relaxed. The record leg also
  cannot be satisfied by an answer the backend wrote, and `TestTheAppliedLambdaFamilyIsOnTheRecord` fails if a row's
  record disappears, so coverage cannot be deleted by deleting a record.
## ADR 0371 — an application that omits a parameter is read against the body's entry tuple (L11.7, Gap R.329, Gap R.334, Gap R.335, 2026-10-19)

- **The arity audit a CALL needs is not the arity audit a CLONE needs.** `print((lambda f, y=10: f(y))(lambda x: x +
  1))` is the reference's `11` and this build refused it, while the twin that writes both arguments answered `10`.
  Nothing about the body differs — the two programs emit the same `define`, and the only difference is how many words
  the application wrote. Two audits were reading the call's argument list as the body's parameter list:
  `len(c.Args) != len(def.Params)` at the site loop, and the `Default != nil` drop inside
  `callableCalledParams`/`lambdaCalledParams`, which removed every defaulted parameter from `calledPos` *before* the
  first audit could even be reached. The second was the deeper one, and it was written for an honest reason — the pass
  had no way to name what a defaulted slot holds — which had simply stopped being true: `resolve` already answers an
  expression with the symbol of the function it names, so a default that IS a function is an entry.
- **An omitted position is read from the parameter, never from the argument.** `callableSiteOperand(c, cf, pos)` takes
  the argument when the call wrote one and the parameter's own `Default` when it did not. That is the same expression
  the body would have seen, and it is the only expression whose symbol can stand in the body's call. The first draft
  kept a `*KeywordArg` unwrap in it, which was dead code — `callableSiteOmission` declines a keyworded call before any
  position is read — and dead code in an audit is a claim that the audit does not cover what it covers.
- **Write only what the last called position forces you to write.** `callableSiteFill` grows the retargeted call up to
  `max(calledPos)` and no further: the placeholder where the clone calls the entry by name and reads nothing, a *copy*
  of the default's expression at a position in between that the body reads, and nothing at or above the last called
  one — the ordinary call road owns the default fill (ADR 0322), and a pass that duplicates that rule owns two rules
  that can disagree. `print((lambda f, k=3, n=40: f(k) + n)(lambda x: x * 2))` → `46` is the witness: the emitted call
  reads `call i32 @gy_…$callable$…(i32 0, i32 3, i32 40)` — the placeholder at the entry's position, the prototype's
  defaults everywhere else, filled by the road that already knew how.
- **Build the new argument list before you touch the node.** The rewrite mutates the AST the planner walked, so a
  `node.Args = append(node.Args, copy)` followed by a bail on a later check leaves a program half-rewritten and
  returns it as `prog, nil` — an "unchanged" program that is not unchanged. The list is now assembled, audited
  (`pos >= len(grown) || grown[pos] == nil` for every called position), and only then assigned.
- **An account field has to separate the programs it claims to separate.** My first `omitted_arguments` counted the
  words the pass *wrote*, and the roadmap's two headline programs — the omission and its twin — both reported `0`,
  because in both cases the call road filled the defaults. The field now counts the parameters the applications left
  out and the pass read off the body (`site.omitted`), which is the fact an agent is asking about; the twin reports
  `0`, the omission `1`, the two-omission program `2`. A machine-readable witness that cannot distinguish the case from
  its control is not a witness.
- **Declines are not refusals, and the account is where they are visible.** The recursion variant — `def run(n,
  f=lambda x: x): return 0 if n == 0 else f(n) + run(n - 1)` — reaches the ordinary road's `"f" is called but is not a
  function …` at the terminal, and only `--callables` says why: `"run" recurses at line 2 without filling every
  parameter positionally`. Both sentences are pinned, one in the refusal table and one over the document, because the
  terminal and the account are allowed to differ and neither is allowed to drift silently (roadmap Gap R.335).
- **Two new rows came out of doing the row, and both are named by their shape.** A body that calls its own parameter
  *while* reading a name from the enclosing frame (`def f(x): return (lambda h: h(1) + x)(lambda q: q * 10)`, the
  reference's `12`) is **Gap R.334** — the clone road and the capture road were built in the same cycle and never met,
  `cloneCallable` minting the entry parameters while `captureParamWord` decides the captures, neither consulting the
  other. The recursion variant is **Gap R.335**. Each half of R.334 answers on its own, which is the localisation, and
  each was written as a refusal row naming its row before it was written down anywhere else.
- **The record leg had nothing to check.** Not one of the `lambda f, y=10` family was in
  `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden.json`, so a table over them would have "passed" by comparing nothing; six
  sources went to the recorder (`tools/recmerge`, 7827 → 7833) and `TestTheAppliedLambdaFamilyIsOnTheRecord` fails if
  any of them is missing. `integration/programs/lambda_applied_entry_tuple.gy` joined the matrix (222 → 223 programs,
  209 → 210 rows), and the Snapshot row's numbers are the artifact's — the guard quoted the right ones back at me and
  editing the prose is the fix, not relaxing the test.

## ADR 0372 — a clone carries the entries its calls name AND the names its body reads (L11.7, Gap R.334, Gap R.336, Gap R.337, 2026-10-19)

- **Two roads built in one cycle are not one road.** ADR 0370 gave an applied `lambda` its clone (parameters for the
  entries its calls name, from `calledPos`) and gave a hoisted `lambda` its captures (a parameter per free name, via
  `captureParamWord`) — and no body was ever asked for both, because the entry audit declined the program before the
  capture road was consulted. `def f(x): return (lambda h: h(1) + x)(lambda q: q * 10)` is the reference's `12`, and the
  two halves answered `8` and `10` on the same build; that contrast was the whole localisation, and the fix was the
  union the row's own plan had already named. The lesson generalises: when a pass grows a second property, ask which
  body needs BOTH, and write that program first.
- **The moment a fact can be read is part of the design.** The capture list is `lambdaFrameCaptures`'s answer, and that
  question needs the frame the APPLICATION is written in — which only exists inside the pass, at the site, with
  `r.encs[rank]` in hand. Asking it at emission time is asking it after the caller has been forgotten; asking it twice
  in two places is two answers. So the pass asks the closure road's own reader and ships the answer on the node it
  minted (`FuncDef.Captures`, `json:"-"` beside `SkipEmit` and `CloneOf`: `--emit-ast` and `gusty fmt` speak the source,
  ADR 0320), and `GenerateIRReport` puts it in `g.lambdaCaptures` before the first call is lowered — the same
  "asked of the program, not of the emission order" rule the pair-arity and container-answer scans already read by.
- **Never grow a parameter list the source wrote.** My first draft appended the capture parameters to the enclosing
  `def`'s own `Params`, and `def h(a, b): return (lambda f: f(a) + b)(lambda z: z * 2)` died with
  `codegen: missing argument "b" for h`: the emitter was checking `h(3, 4)` against a prototype nobody wrote, and the
  error named a parameter of the caller for a problem in a clone. Only the GENERATED declaration may grow, and every
  audit needs to know which parameters the human typed — hence `callableFn.srcParams`, which the ADR 0371 arity rules
  now read instead of `len(def.Params)`.
- **A capture is filled with the caller's word, not with the value.** The emitted call for `def h(a, b)` reads
  `call i32 @gy_h$lambda$…$callable$…(i32 0, i32 %p0, i32 %p1)`: the ADR 0371 placeholder at the entry and the caller's
  own parameter words for the captures. Copying the value would print the same bytes for every program in the tables and
  be wrong for the ones that rebind the local after the application — and it would need a word per kind, which is
  L11.1's unmade machinery. Fidelity to the caller's read is also what keeps a captured local alive across the call.
- **Determinism is a property of a list order, not of a hash function.** The capture list is sorted before it becomes
  parameters; a map iteration would mint a different `define` per run and break the pass's own hash test (ADR 0273's
  statelessness, which `--callables`' digest is the witness for).
- **An account field earns its place by separating the case from its control.** `capture_parameters` is `0` for
  `(lambda f: f(3))(lambda x: x * 2)`, `1` for this row's program, `2` for the two-capture one. Without it, `clones:1`,
  `rewritten:true` and a hash described ADR 0370's self-contained clone and this clone identically, and an agent reading
  the JSON could not tell which road answered.
- **A refusal the reader sees can be a different sentence from the one the compiler knows, and both must be pinned.**
  The entry-side twin — `def use(seed): base = 1; return apply1(lambda x: x + base, seed)`, the reference's `4` — is
  declined by the pass, whose account now says `an entry lambda reads "base" from the frame its application is written
  in … (Gap R.336)`, while the terminal still prints the ordinary road's `"fn" is called but is not a function …
  (roadmap L11.1, ADR 0166)`, because `defunctionalizeCallables` swallows the decline and the emitter says what IT knows.
  The old decline sentence (`a lambda passed to a parameter reads that parameter's function`) described none of these
  programs — the name belongs to the caller, not the callee — so it was replaced with one that names the word and the
  row, and the gap between the two surfaces is filed as **Gap R.337** rather than fixed under this row's name: it
  changes no decision, and pretending otherwise would have made ADR 0372's tables untestable.
- **The declined shape is where the next row lives, and it lives on the OTHER side of the same union.** The body side
  reads the caller's frame through a capture parameter; the ENTRY side cannot, because ADR 0345 made an entry a bare
  symbol. Giving an entry captures means the callee's clone carries them too and the clone's identity becomes the pair
  (entry symbols, each entry's capture list), not the tuple ADR 0345/0364 hash. That is **Gap R.336**, and the hard
  spelling — `def stepper(): … (lambda fn: fn(2) + shift)(lambda n: n * step)`, where the body reads `shift` (R.334's,
  answers) and the entry reads `step` (R.336's, declines), and an all-or-nothing pass hands the whole program to the
  ordinary road — is pinned instead of a soft one, because the soft one could be closed by accident.
- **The record leg again had nothing to check.** None of the six union shapes was in
  `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden.json`; ten sources went to `tools/recmerge` (7833 → 7844, five new), and one
  candidate never got a record at all: the two-frames-up program is refused by this backend, so the recorder refuses to
  write it — which is the rule that keeps a divergence on the table instead of in a file.
  `integration/programs/lambda_applied_capture_entry.gy` joined the matrix (223 → 224 programs, 210 → 211 rows,
  178 → 179 asserted, 164 → 165 oracle `match`), and the Snapshot's numbers moved because the artifact said they should.

## ADR 0373 — the return word of a float-answering body comes from the body, not from its parameter list (L11.6 · Gap R.3c, Gap R.338, Gap R.339, 2026-10-19)

- **A guard can be a hypothesis wearing a coat.** `returnedFloatRebindings` — the gate ADR 0254 built so
  a function's return word stops coming from the *shape* of its `return` line — opened with
  `if fd == nil || len(fd.Params) == 0 { return nil }`. The scan is about the NAME the return reads back;
  where the name came from is a different question. `def f(): u = 9.5 / return u` is the first float
  function anybody writes, and this backend printed `0` at exit 0 — `define i32 @gy_f()` over a body
  that had just executed `store double`, the read answering the double's low word. Deleting the guard was
  one line; the row is about noticing that the guard had no reason attached to it.
- **The wrong answer was two deep, and the second one only appeared once the first was gone.** With the
  guard removed, `return u` answered `9.5` and `v = u * 2` / `return v` still printed `0` — and kept
  printing `0` even with a parameter in the signature, which is the tell that the SCAN was broken and not
  the parameter list. `v` is a double only because `u` is one, and the scan asked `isFloat` of each
  binding once, in Go's map order. Repetition to a fixed point, over a per-round snapshot, is four lines
  and is order-independent; a single pass is a coin flip you can't reproduce in a bug report.
- **"Was it EVER a float" is the wrong question, and the wrong answer to it is the same bug backwards.**
  The scan keeps the LAST binding of each name, because the read answers the last write's word:
  `u = 2.5` / `u = 3` / `return u` must answer `3`, and the "any binding" version prints `3.0`. The unit
  table pins both, and the IR table pins `define double`/`ret double` on one side and `define i32` with
  no `ret double` on the other — a gate that promoted everything containing an `alloca double` would pass
  the value table and be wrong in the other direction.
- **One table, one answer, again (ADR 0273, read by a new road).** `floatReboundReturnAsksForTheDouble`
  had been building a copy-add-restore of `floatVars` privately. That is now `withFloatNames`, and the
  scan asks its questions inside it, so `funcReturnsFloat`'s answer about a body, `isFloat`'s answer about
  one of its expressions, and the assignment road's decision mid-emission are three readings of one map.
  The `return -x` story in Gap R.3c — a `define double` with an `ret i32`, `llc` rejecting the module — is
  what you get when they are not, and it is why the method road now passes the same helper instead of
  asking the question cold.
- **The conformance program is a lie detector, and this time it caught ME.** `float_answer_word.gy` was
  written with a `lastWrite` group in it; `TestConformanceMatrix` failed it with
  `aot="…3.0…" python="…3…"`. That is a real wrong answer at exit 0 — pre-existing (the pre-ADR-0373
  build prints the same `3.0`), and caused by `g.floatVars` being ONE MAP FOR THE WHOLE MODULE: the
  assignment road notes "this name's last write was a double" as it emits and nothing clears the note at
  the next `define`, so what an earlier body bound decides what a later body's same-named name IS. The
  group was cut out of the asserted program and filed as **Gap R.339** with the reference's bytes pinned
  beside today's in `TestWhatTheFloatAnswerWordStillOwesIsFiledNotFixed`; the ledger was not edited to
  accept `3.0`. Had I written the roadmap prose instead of the program, this would have shipped.
- **The record leg had nothing to check, again.** None of the fourteen float-return shapes was in
  `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden.json`; they went through `tools/recmerge` (the record to **7858**
  sources), each recorded from the reference with the compiled leg cross-checked before the entry was
  written — and the test that asks the record leg fails if NO row of its table is covered, so the guard
  cannot quietly become a no-op.
- **A parallel subtest is a counter you never read.** `if asked == 0 { t.Fatal(...) }` after a loop of
  `t.Run(func(t){ t.Parallel() … })` reports "the record leg is not being walked" on a green run, because
  the subtests have not started by the time the loop returns. Counters that a guard reads belong in serial
  subtests.
- **The probe binary has to be rebuilt before it is trusted, and a probe you did not rebuild is not
  evidence.** This cycle carried a working note claiming module-level floats were folded into compiled
  bodies and that a `def f(): u = RATE` program answered; the tree has no such code (`git diff` showed
  three files, none of them the module road), and the probe outputs that "proved" it came from a
  `/tmp/gustyc` built at some earlier state. The behaviour that matters here was re-measured twice with
  freshly built binaries — `-tags=llvm20` and untagged agree, byte for byte — and the module-float row
  (Gap R.35) is still 🟨 `PARTIAL`, not "done", which is what the tracker now says.
- **Filed rather than absorbed:** the method whose body binds its own name to a double (a method's return
  word is fixed with the receiver's), the dead `alloca double` a body leaves when the float binding is
  overwritten before the return (Gap R.290's family), `def twice(): return half() + half()` (Gap R.331's
  return-kind registration), and the module-wide float table (Gap R.339) — each with its own row, its own
  sentence, and a test that fails when it closes.

## ADR 0374 — a conditional expression runs the arm its test chose (Gap R.340, 2026-10-18)

- **A door nothing calls is a hypothesis, not a change.** This cycle inherited `pkg/lang/ternary_arms.go`
  already written — `ternaryBranch`, the gate, the silence list, four tables of tests, an ADR — and
  `go build ./...` green, because a method nobody calls compiles as happily as one everybody calls. The
  tell was that the new tests failed exactly as the defect predicts (`boom\n1\n`, `want "1\n"`): the two
  lowerings that answer a ternary, `ternaryI32` and `ternaryDouble`, still lowered both arms beside the test
  and folded the pair into one `select`. Before believing any file that arrives already written, ask which
  call site reaches it: `grep -rn ternaryBranch pkg/lang` answered in one second what an hour of reading the
  door could not.
- **A `select` is the bug whenever an arm is a program.** Both operands of a `select` are *arguments*, so the
  run time executed both arms to answer one of them. `print(1 if x > 0 else boom())` printed `boom`,
  `print(1 if x > 0 else 1 // 0)` raised from the arm the test had already rejected, and — the face that
  turned a wrong answer into a compiler bug — `def fact(n): return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1)` never
  returned, because the recursive call sat unconditionally in the block with the test: the base case was a
  value and not a stop, the root stack filled, and the harness reported a dead artifact at **exit 2**. The
  fix is not new machinery — it is ADR 0275's `logicSkeleton` for the construct that has an arm on each side
  of the test.
- **The gate's default has to be the expensive direction, because "has an effect" is not a node type here.**
  The first cut of the gate asked "is the arm a call", and that is the gate that would have shipped the
  `1 // 0` program: a division raises with no call in sight, and so do `xs[9]`, `d["k"]`, an ordering of two
  kinds, a container literal's allocation, a comprehension's loop. So the list is inverted — an arm may be
  folded only when it is provably a value and nothing else (a literal, a name the checker proves written,
  `+ - * & | ^ << >>` and the six orderings over literals of one domain, `not`/unary minus of a literal) —
  and everything else costs five labels and a `phi`. ADR 0273's rule kept the fold where it is free: the
  pure-pair `select` is pinned in *both* directions, present in one test and `tern.merge` forbidden in it.
- **An `UnboundLocalError` is an effect, and asking the written-slot question twice asks it wrongly.**
  `if flag:` / `y = 7` / `return (1 if flag else y) + 0` raised for a name the taken arm never mentions,
  because the ADR 0228 flag test is emitted where the read is lowered and a `select`'s operands all dominate
  its test. `readMayTrap` reads `boundFlags`/`boundSlots` — the same tables `checkBound` consults — rather
  than keeping a second opinion about which reads can trap (ADR 0273 again: one table, one answer).
- **A `phi` needs two things a `select` never did.** Its incoming block must be a real predecessor, and an
  arm whose lowering contains a call does not end where the door left it: the call road closes with an
  `@exn_flag` test that branches to the enclosing function's raise-exit or to a fresh continuation block.
  The one-instruction forwarding blocks (`tern.thenfwd`, `tern.elsefwd`) solve both at once, and they are
