  what make a trap in a rejected arm impossible instead of merely unobserved — the raise unwinds with the
  frames the arm's own call pushed, so `rt_die` still prints `in boom` for the arm that really ran.
- **A conformance program is a lie detector that also fires on your neighbours.** `programs/ternary_arms.gy`
  failed the matrix with `aot=""`: `def scaled(n): return 0.0 if n == 0 else 1.5 + scaled(n - 1)` written
  above `def fact(n): return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1)` made `fact`'s arms "disagree on a word",
  because the two bodies share a parameter NAME and `g.floatVars` is one map for the whole module — the
  measurement **Gap R.339** already owns. The honest options were the program's spelling or the ledger, and I
  took the program's: each function now spells its own parameter (`step`, `count`, `value`), the reason is
  written in the program's header comment and in the ADR, and no expectation was edited to make `fact` look
  right. Reordering the same two functions on a pre-change build reproduced it, which is how I know the row
  it belongs to is R.339 and not this one.
- **The branch does not rescue a container arm, and saying so is part of landing it.**
  `[1, 2] if c > 0 else [3]` still reaches `llc` as `phi i32 [ @.lst1, %tern.thenfwd ], [ @.lst2,
  %tern.elsefwd ]` — the same literal-global-in-value-position operand Gap R.128 has pinned since it was
  filed, now arriving through a `phi` instead of a `select`. Same probe, same exit 2, same owner (L11.1's
  tagged handle); the probe was not re-pinned, because nothing about its answer changed.
- **Differential-build the refusal you add.** A new refusal sentence can turn a program that compiles today
  into exit 1, so each table was run through a `git worktree` build of `HEAD` beside the working tree before
  anything was believed about which shapes changed answer. That is also how the shared-name `fact`/`scaled`
  refusal was proved pre-existing rather than a regression from this door.
- **The record leg had nothing to check — again — and `tools/recmerge` is the only way to give it something.**
  None of the 34 untaken-arm/recursion/trap programs was in `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden.json`;
  `goldenStdoutIs`/`goldenRunError` fail on a *missing* record, so the tests were red until the recorder ran,
  and it refuses an entry the compiled leg will not agree to (record: **7892**). Four of the 34 are trap
  rows: the entry carries CPython's class and sentence, which is what makes "the branch swallowed the raise"
  a failing case rather than a passing one.
- **Every count in the docs is the artifact's, and five guards say so.** Adding 34 sources, one ADR and one
  conformance program moved `AGENTS.md`, `docs/operations.md`, and the Snapshot's record / ADR / program /
  matrix / oracle / queue rows; `golden_artifact_counts_test.go`, `docs_artifact_counts_test.go` and
  `roadmap_snapshot_test.go` failed until each cell matched the file, which is the cheapest possible price
  for a table that says "measured, not remembered".
## ADR 0375 — the float-variable table a body reads is that body's own writes (L11.6 · Gap R.339; two rows filed)

- **The bug was found by the matrix, and by nothing else.** `print(bound()) / print(lastWrite())`
  printed `3.0` where CPython prints `3`, and every single-function case in the suite agreed with
  CPython, because each of them asks ONE function at a time. An order-dependent answer is invisible to
  a test that asks one thing at a time — the only witness that puts several bodies in one file is the
  conformance matrix, which is why `float_answer_word.gy` is where the pair was found (it failed the
  matrix, got cut out of the asserted program, and became Gap R.339 with the reference's bytes beside
  today's). **Lesson kept:** when a defect is "the answer depends on what else is in the file", the
  regression suite must be a program, not a table of isolated snippets.
- **Prefer the mechanism the codebase already trusts over a hand-rolled one.** My first patch swapped
  the float table inside `funcDef` — it fixed the reported program and left the *rule* false, because
  the method emitter and the closure lift emit bodies without ever going through `funcDef`. The module
  already has `beginScope()` ("which names are containers … are facts about a single scope") installing
  the container/bool/None/text tables, and `enterBody()` for the two roads that skip it; putting the
  float table (and its `doubleSlot` companion) in both, behind one helper in `float_frame.go`, is the
  version the method rows in the answer table accept. **Writing the witness table before choosing the
  fix is what caught the half-open version** — `a method's float local is not the next function's float`
  fails the `funcDef`-only patch.
- **Read the row's own Definition-of-done before writing tests.** Gap R.339's Evidence cell already
  said the filed table is "DELETED when its rows agree, and `float_answer_word.gy` regains the
  `lastWrite` group it lost". Honouring that literally was the difference between a fix and a fix plus
  the restored witness: the pair is back in the asserted program, the filed test is gone, and the IR
  claim (`define double @gy_a()` / `define i32 @gy_b()` / `define double @gy_c()` in one module) is
  what stops a future "fix" that only redirects the printer.
- **Two agents in one checkout is a hazard, and `git add -A` is the sharp end of it.** The previous
  cycle's commit swept *another agent's* in-flight files into it because the whole tree was staged. This
  cycle ran in its own `git worktree` off `HEAD` (`git worktree add ../gusty-r339 -b cycle/r339-head`),
  with explicit paths staged and never `-A`, so neither agent could contaminate the other's commit.
  Related courtesy: **0374 was left unclaimed** — the applied-`lambda` rows already in flight cite that
  number in three source comments — and this row took 0375, with the reason written into the ADR header.
- **The artifact owns its own formatting; use the tool that writes it.** Deleting one stale record entry
  with `json.load`/`json.dump` re-wrote all 52k lines of `interpreter-golden.json` (Go's encoder and
  Python's disagree about escapes and indentation) and `git checkout` was the only clean way back.
  `tools/recmerge` *appends into the record's own text* "so no existing byte moves" — the fix for a stale
  entry is to never write it (rename the source before recording, then record the one text you want).
- **`recmerge` refuses what the tracker still owes.** Gap R.341's `def loopAcc(): … / print(loopAcc())`
  could not be recorded (`got "0"`, `want "6.0"`) — which is the record doing its job: an entry is
  written from the reference only with the compiled leg agreeing. Those shapes live in the filed tables,
  with a guard that fails if the answer moves in EITHER direction (including into a refusal, which for a
  wrong value would be a new defect).
- **`cliRunCode` sees stdout; diagnostics are on stderr.** Two filed rows "failed" with an empty
  message because they grepped the captured stdout for `Gap R.35` / the `llc` sentence. Exit codes come
  from `cliRunCode`, sentences come from `cliRun` (`CombinedOutput`). Pin both, from the right helper.
- **Let the count guards edit the docs for you.** `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered`,
  `TestTheArtifactTableCountsAreTheFilesOwn`, `TestTheRecordedSourceCountInTheAgentFacingDocsIsTheFilesOwn`,
  `TestTheCLISuitesArtifactCountsAreTheFilesOwn` and `TestTheRecordCountTheCLIKitQuotesIsTheFilesOwn` each
  name the file and the stale number (`docs/operations.md says 7858 sources … the file holds 7872`). Run
  them first, patch what they name, and the docs cannot drift from the artifacts.
- **Same-package helpers collide with test helpers.** `firstLine` already existed in `oracle.go`; a
  test-file helper needs a name the package does not already use (`headLineOf`). `go vet` finds this
  before `go test` runs anything.
- **Filed rather than absorbed:** **Gap R.341** (a `for`-driven float accumulator inside a body prints
  `0`, the same loop at module level prints `6.0`) and **Gap R.342** (a nested `def` sharing a name with
  its enclosing body's float local stores through the *enclosing* frame's alloca — `llc` rejects the
  module, exit 2, ADR 0166's code for a compiler bug). Both measured identical before and after this
  change; `allocd` was deliberately NOT folded into the new helper, because bundling it would have made
  the commit two rules and hidden which one a green test was proving.

## ADR 0379 — the pass's decline is quoted beside the call it refused (L11.7 · Gap R.337, 2026-10-19)

- **A correct rewrite rule can be a lossy diagnostic, and the loss is invisible to every test that
  only checks the answer.** `defunctionalizeCallables` handing back the untouched program is ADR 0345's
  all-or-nothing rule and exactly right; the fact that the sentence explaining WHY never reached the
  terminal was invisible to 40+ refusal rows that each asserted `strings.Contains(msg, want)` — the
  generic sentence was in the message, so every row was green while the reader was sent to read the
  wrong ADR (`L11.1`, which owns nothing in a program whose only problem is an ENTRY reading its
  caller's frame). The row that knew the answer (`Gap R.336`) was named only inside `--callables`, which
  nobody consults from a terminal. **Lesson kept:** when a refusal is "correct", ask what the reader
  learns from it, not only whether the row's substring is present.
- **Pin the absence, or the append is unconditional.** The first patch appended the decline whenever
  the pass had spoken, and every new case passed. The row's own Definition of done contains the second
  half — *a program the pass never spoke about keeps the generic sentence byte for byte* — and writing
  that case is what found the bug in the fix: the pass's "no function calls its own parameter, …"
  decline is true of EVERY first-order program, including `t = 1 / print(t())`, so a quotation stamped
  on that refusal would talk about a pass that had nothing to say while destroying a sentence agents
  match on. The answer was a field (`noWork` on `*callableDecline`), not a prose comparison — a
  decline that is a fact about the pass must not be classified by string equality with the pass's own
  wording, which any edit to that wording would silently reclassify.
- **Two faces of one compile need one owner for a sentence.** `--callables` had
  "the rewrite was withdrawn: …" as a literal inside the reporter; the terminal needed the same words.
  Pulling them into `callableRewriteWithdrawn()` — one function, both callers — is what lets the test
  assert `strings.Contains(refusal, account.refused[0])` byte for byte instead of hoping. The same rule
  covers the plan-time decline: `defunctionalizeCallablesTelling` returns `err.Error()`, the very method
  the account prints, so the two cannot drift even though they are produced in different places.
- **The quotation must not move the capability code.** ADR 0346's classifier matches markers and takes
  the longest, so appending a sentence is exactly how `lower.unsupported.indirect-call` can silently
  become some other row's code — an agent's branch stops firing and nothing goes red. Every row of both
  new files therefore asserts the code for the LONGER message, and the CLI file asserts it out of the
  `--json` payload rather than the library. A quotation is not a new shape; the tests are what make that
  a fact rather than an intention.
- **The all-or-nothing pass has two ways back to the untouched tree, and only one had a sentence.** The
  plan-time decline (`planDefunctionalization` returns `*callableDecline`) and the post-write invariant
  (`callableNoFunctionValuesLeft` fails, `applyDefunctionalization` returns `prog, nil`) are different
  failures; the second was reported only by a string literal in the JSON reporter. `writeDefunctionalization`
  was extracted so both entry points share the writing, and the withdrawal is now a decline in the same
  shape — which is also the reason the table for "what the pass hands back" has four rows and not two.
- **Byte-for-byte means written out, not imported from the road.** The control rows compare against a
  sentence spelled out in the test file, so editing `callBuiltins`' message fails a case. A helper that
  rebuilt the expectation from the same format string would have made the guard tautological.
- **The record leg needs the same discipline as the fix.** Two of the four rewritten regression programs
  had never been recorded; `tools/recmerge` added them (7947 → 7949) with the compiled leg
  cross-checked, and the record-leg test fails if NO row of its table matches a record entry — a table
  that silently skips everything is a leg that stopped walking.
- **Worktree discipline held.** This cycle ran in its own `git worktree` off `HEAD`
  (`gusty-round3`, branch `cycle/round3-head`) with explicit paths staged and never `-A`, because a
  second agent is mid-flight in `../gusty-r339`. `push` remains impossible from this sandbox:
  `sign_and_send_pubkey: signing failed for ED25519 … agent refused operation`, and `gh` is unauthenticated
  — so the commits stay local and the branch is the artifact.

## ADR 0380 — a capture travels one step: the frame that owns a name answers for the one below it (L11.7 · Gap R.330, 2026-10-19)

- **A gate is a question, and a question can be aimed at the wrong table.** The refusal read like an honest door —
  「a capture crosses as one i32 word, which cannot say what the value is… a value no call in the program can be
  asked about」 — and it was a true statement about the *scan* and a false one about the *value*. A capture parameter
  is a position the source never wrote: `lambdaCallArgs` appends it to a copy of the call at emission time, so
  `callArgAt` can never find it. Two frames deep worked only by accident (the forwarded name sat beside a position the
  outer application filled). **Lesson kept:** when a gate says "nothing can tell me", ask whether the gate is asking a
  position that exists in its own data model, or one it invented downstream. The fix was not to weaken the gate — it was
  to ask the frame that SUPPLIES the value, which had answered the question all along.
- **Forward a verdict, never a permission.** The tempting one-liner was "a forwarded capture is a parameter, and
  parameters are the caller's business — skip the check". Because the record I keep is the *verdict* the supplying frame
  reached (`kind`, `carries`) rather than a boolean "allowed", a text/float/container at the bottom of a chain is refused
  exactly as it is one frame up. Three new refusal rows exist for that reason alone, and they are the rows that make the
  "no new wrong answers at exit 0" claim checkable rather than rhetorical.
- **A scan that reports through a binder is a bug waiting for the door that reads it.** `scanFreeIn`'s `*Lambda` arm
  handed the walk to `lambdaFreeNames`, which seeds binders with the NESTED lambda's parameters only — so the enclosing
  body reported a name it binds itself as free in itself. Nothing noticed for as long as the road existed because the
  only consumer was a gate that refused first. The symptom, once the gate was fixed, was perfect: `multiple values for
  argument "y"`, a CPython sentence spoken by a compiler that had minted `%p0` and `%p2` both named `y`. **Lesson
  kept:** when fixing a gate, expect the door behind it to speak; the gate's silence is not evidence about the road.
- **The reference's own error messages are a compiler's best free test oracle.** Both defects this cycle found announced
  themselves with CPython sentences — `multiple values for argument` (duplicate forwarded parameter) and `undefined
  name` (filed as Gap R.348). A refusal whose wording belongs to the language is a signal that the compiler is
  describing its own bookkeeping in the program's vocabulary.
- **Pin the pre-existing control beside the newly-reachable wrong answer.** Unlocking the gate made one program compile
  that prints `0` where the reference prints `[111, 111]` — a container answered by the outermost of three lambdas. The
  one-frame spelling (`print((lambda x: [x for q in [1, 2]])(9))`) prints `0` on the pre-ADR build too, so both are filed
  (Gap R.331's answer-kind door) with the control in the same table: the row fails in either direction, and the pair is
  what proves the defect is the answer door's rather than this cycle's. It is not on the record — `tools/recmerge` asks
  the reference and cross-checks the compiled leg, and a source whose legs disagree has no answer to write.
- **Write the IR assertion in the emitted language, not in the AST's.** The claim "a capture travels one step" is a fact
  about which registers an inner `call` reads: `call i32 @gy_lambda_2(i32 100, i32 %p1, i32 %p0)` inside
  `define i32 @gy_lambda_1(i32 %p0, i32 %p1)`. Asserting the headers and that every argument register is within the
  enclosing `define`'s arity is checkable without a second model of what forwarding should mean; asserting "the outer
  frame's value reaches the inner body" would have been a claim about the AST that any of three wrong IRs could satisfy.
- **Per-compile state is the rule, again.** The verdict table is keyed by `*FuncDef` and allocated beside
  `g.lambdaOrigin`, because this repository has already removed the package-level version of exactly this shape twice
  (ADR 0343's Gap R.259/R.260). A memo that survives a compile is a memo two compiles can lose an argument with.
- **The row's Definition of done is a test instruction.** Gap R.330 said "the row moves to the answer table with `111`
  as the expectation and the refusal case is DELETED"; doing it in that order (delete the pin, then move the program) is
  what keeps a filed row from quietly becoming a permanent second truth about the language.
- **Worktree discipline held.** This cycle ran in its own `git worktree` off `HEAD` (`gusty-round4`, branch
  `cycle/round4-head`) with explicit paths staged and never `-A`, because two other worktrees (`gusty-r339`,
  `gusty-round3`) carry another agent's in-flight edits. `push` remains impossible from this sandbox
  (`sign_and_send_pubkey: … agent refused operation`, `gh` unauthenticated), so the branch is the artifact.

## ADR 0381 — a comprehension's target is a binding of the frame that hosts it (Gap R.348, 2026-10-20)

- **A file with no callers is a design document, not a feature.** `pkg/lang/frame_targets.go` arrived with ADR 0380
  carrying the whole rule — the counter, the release, the predicate, the per-frame entry wired into `beginScope` and
  `enterBody` — and nothing called the writer or the reader. The row read as "half-implemented"; the honest reading is
  "described, not wired", and the distinction changed what I looked for: not a bug in a rule, but the two call sites the
  rule was written to have. Revert-and-measure proved it: with the two `note/forget` calls and the one `frameOwnsTarget`
  ask removed, the three DoD programs print `undefined name "x"` and nothing else changes.
- **Ask whether the "before" output was ever measured, before quoting it.** I began this cycle carrying a note (mine,
  from earlier in the session) that said the failure came out of codegen with a `(hint: …)` clause and that the top-level
  bare-expression spelling answered `[11, 21]`. Re-running the probe showed the hint text exists nowhere in the tree and
  the bare expression does answer — a fold path — while the `print(...)` form did not. Two of my three remembered facts
  were plausible inventions; the third was real. Everything in the ADR and the roadmap row is output I ran in this turn.
- **Build the baseline in a worktree, or you will compare against yourself.** `git stash` + rebuild did not give me a
  pre-change binary: `frame_targets.go` is untracked, so the stashed tree still had it and would not compile. `git worktree
  add /tmp/base 946b272` gave the real "before", and it is what proved the five neighbours (R.349–R.353) are not mine —
  including the `[[y for y in [1, 2]] for x in [10, 20]]` face, which is exit 2 on the baseline and stays exit 2.
- **A conformance program is a witness, not a scratch pad.** The DoD asked me to put the chain in a comprehension inside
  `lambda_capture_chain.gy`; the extra witness I liked (`x = 1000` beside the comprehension, to pin the nearer-binding
  rule) poisoned the whole file — every capture named `x` in the program started reading the module's global and the
  matrix's program printed `1110` for `111`. Removing it was right twice over: the file prints line for line what the
  reference prints again, and the poisoning shape is a real defect with a real name (Gap R.349) that I would have hidden
  inside a green program.
- **The recorder is the review.** Eleven sources went to `tools/recmerge`. The `x = 5` one came back refused *before* the
  fix, because CPython says `[11, 21]` and the compiled leg said `[6, 6]`; after the fix it was accepted. That single
  tool behaviour is a better proof of a wrong-answer fix than any assertion I could have written in the test.
- **Table-shaped docs have failure modes only a scanner finds.** Two of my five new queue rows used `Pri` labels
  (`160aa`, `160ab`) outside `queuePri`'s `^[0-9]+[a-z]?$`, and the snapshot scanner stopped at them: the tracker
  reported 214 rows where the file held 259 and 45 rows of owed work went invisible. The guard failed loudly and named the
  shape (that is what `countQueueRows`'s `hidden` tally exists for, ADR 0343's cycle); the lesson is to run
  `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered` immediately after inserting rows, not at the end.
- **`--callables` said nothing changed, and that is the machine path being honest.** The defunctionalisation pass still
  declines this program — the ordinary lambda road answers it — so the pass report is identical before and after, and
  `--json` carries the answer at `"exit": 0`. A row that changed the emitter rather than the pass should not move the
  pass's numbers, and a cycle that moved them all would be a cycle worth interrogating.
- **Push status.** Same sandbox limitation as the last cycle: `git push origin HEAD` fails with
  `sign_and_send_pubkey: … agent refused operation` (`gh` unauthenticated), so the commit is the artifact and it is
  pushed-or-not reported rather than claimed.

## ADR 0391 — an empty container written as a call is labelled with the kind the object already has (Gap R.360, 2026-10-21)

- **"The tag table has a set in it" is not the same claim as "a slot can say it holds a set."** I started this
  cycle expecting to write a set tag. `value.go` has had `TagSet` since the beginning, `@rt_pair_truth` has had
  its container arm since ADR 0275, and the container printer has read slot tags since ADR 0232 — none of that
  mattered, because the road that *writes* a slot asks `elemKindTag`, that predicate reads spellings, and `set()`
  is a `*Call`. It fell through to `return int32(TagInt), true`. The defect was one `return` line away from a
  helper I did not have to change. Reading the store road to its last line was the whole fix.
- **Ask which road misinformed the other.** `print(len(xs[0]))` over `xs = [set()]` raised `TypeError: object of
  type 'int' has no len()`. That message is not confusion — `len` asked the tag and answered it exactly. A trap
  that names a kind the program never wrote is the cheapest possible proof of a label that lies, cheaper than the
  wrong print beside it, because a print can be blamed on the printer. Two of the six probe programs were the
  same defect wearing a raise.
- **The gate list is the bug list.** Before the change, `taggableNestedElem`, `foldArgCarriesAContainer`,
  `isContainerExpr` and the print gate all asked `emptyContainerLiteral`, while `elemKindTag`,
  `literalNeedsHeap` and `literalNeedsTags` asked spellings. That is ADR 0232's "one question, asked once" with
  the two halves on opposite sides, and ADR 0259's bool is the identical shape ("the tag table grew a bool and
  only one of the three spellings noticed"). The lesson to keep: when a gate grows an arm, grep for every other
  road that asks the same question. `literalNeedsHeap` had eight call sites — the print door, the slice door,
  the `match` door, the value door, the container-return door — and all eight already paired it with a
  `g.`-method; widening one of them would have left six roads still asking the spelling.
- **`literalNeedsHeap` becoming a method is the tell, not the refactor.** Eight call sites already paired it
  with a `g.`-method (`g.literalNeedsTags`, `g.literalHasPairElement`). A gate that cannot ask the generator
  whether the program defined `set` itself cannot ask the whole question, and the shadow arm is precisely what
  keeps `def set(): return 1` answering `[1]` instead of `[set()]`. The one test that called the free function
  directly now calls `(&irGen{}).literalNeedsHeap(e)` — a zero generator answers the shape, and the four new
  spellings pinned in that table cost nothing and fail the day someone re-splits the door.
- **Refuse consistently, not locally.** `{set(): 1}` printed `{set(): 1}` after the tag landed — a *nicer* wrong
  answer than the `{1: 1}` it had printed, and still wrong where CPython raises `unhashable type: 'set'`. The
  house answer for a container key is the sentence `{[1]: 1}` gives, so the call spelling now gives that
  sentence too, with `exprSnippet` naming "an empty set" instead of `*lang.Call`. A fix that makes one wrong
  answer prettier has not finished; the honest version of "we refuse this shape" has to cover the shape, not the
  spelling it arrived in.
- **The recorder is the review, again.** 41 sources went to `tools/recmerge` and none was refused — which is the
  only proof on offer that a wrong answer moved *toward* the reference rather than to a new wrong place. Three
  pins from ADR 0388 (`TestTheTruthOfASetEntryIsStillAskedOfTheHandle`) were deleted, not updated: their text
  said "flip these to answers", and a kept pin is a second truth.
- **Filed rather than absorbed, twice over.** `len(set())`, `list() == []`, `set() == set()` at exit 0 and
  `abs(list())` at exit 0 are the same missing arm one door further on — `staticContainerKind` and
  `containerHandleOf`, which the `len`/comparison/`abs` gates consult. Opening them means giving the *build* door
  the same arm, and a decide door that opens without its build twin is how you turn refusals into exit-2 modules.
  That is its own row (**Gap R.364**) with all ten shapes pinned at today's bytes, rather than a second feature
  smuggled into this commit.
- **Push status.** Same sandbox limitation as the last cycles: `git push origin HEAD` fails with
  `sign_and_send_pubkey: … agent refused operation` (`gh` unauthenticated), so the commit is the artifact and it
  is reported as pushed-or-not rather than claimed.

## ADR 0392 — the doors that decide an empty container's kind ask the door the roads that store it ask (Gap R.364, 2026-10-21)

- **A gate and its neighbouring door are the same question in two places, and the fix lands twice or it has not
  landed.** ADR 0391 fixed the store roads and left `len(set())`, `list() == []`, `abs(list())` and
  `set() == set()` behind, because this backend asks a container value twice: once through the pair that DECIDES
  (`staticContainerKind` then `containerHandleOf`, ADR 0333's rule that the two are one pair) and once through
  the predicate that STORES (`elemKindTag`). Writing the second and not the first is what produced four
  symptoms from one value.
- **Read a function's tail before believing its switch.** `isContainerExpr` ends with
  `_, ok := emptyContainerLiteral(e); return ok` — the shape WAS known there. The `case *Call:` above it returns
  `false` for any callee the container-answer scan does not name, so the tail was dead code for every call. A
  unit test on the predicate alone ("is `set()` a container?") would have caught this in one line; the bug survived
  because every consumer reached it through a switch arm that answered first.
- **A refusal can be worse than an answer, and the direction of the ladder has to be checked per program.**
  `list() + [1]` had been raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s)` — a raise the reference does not make
  for `[] + [1]`. The "before" of a shape is not automatically honest; I only found it because I diffed pre/post
  over a probe corpus rather than trusting my filed table, which had recorded the refusal as if it were the
  reference's behaviour.
- **Exit-0 numbers are the class this repo files first.** `set() == set()` printing `False` and `abs(list())`
  printing `0` were invisible for the whole time the row was open — no stderr, no diagnostic, exit code
  `success`. Both were pinned with their bytes in the filed table, which is the only reason they were
  interesting enough to fix in the next cycle rather than invisible forever.
- **Diff, then count, then trust.** `print(set() < set())` answering `True` against the reference's `False` looked
  like a regression from this commit and was not: three binaries at three states of the tree all answered `True`.
  Attribution before action is what kept the row honest — the missing piece is `rt_container_order`, which the
  *literal* pair `{1} < {1, 2}` also lacks, so it is Gap R.175's helper, not this row's spelling.
- **Pins are deleted, not annotated.** Four rows in the filed table were removed as their own text required, and
  the integration refusal table lost its two `len` rows; the table keeps `sum(list())` — pinned beside the
  identical refusal `sum(xs)` gives a container VARIABLE, which is the sentence that proves the refusal is the
  fold door's and not this row's.
- **`tools/recmerge` is the reviewer.** 28 sources went in (22 answers + 6 traps), none refused. A trap source
  whose compiled class or message disagrees with CPython's is rejected by the recorder, so "the raise is the
  reference's raise" is a claim the artifact carries, not a claim I make in an ADR.
- **Push status.** `git push origin HEAD` worked this cycle (`f3e67ed..dc15588` for the first row); the sandbox
  limitation reported in earlier cycles is reported when it bites, never assumed.

## ADR 0393 — a condition asks a parameter the kind its caller supplied (Gap R.361 + Gap R.365, 2026-10-22)

- **A gate needs two halves, and the second one is the half that stops a hang.** Pair-bound truth is decided by
  `taggedOrigin` in the first draft — ask the table for a name the ARGUMENT road bound, and stop. That is right
  and not safe: the tag word has exactly one writer (`bindPairParams`), so a body that rebinds its own
  parameter leaves a tag describing a value nothing holds, and the truth road then calls `rt_heap_len` on a word
  that is no longer a handle. Three probes went from *wrong answer* to *run that never ends* while I was writing
  this row — `while v:` … `v = []` counts iterations forever, and the linked binary (same module through `cc`)
  has to be killed. The gate now reads the origin AND the body (`bodyKeepsTheEntryPair`), and an unknown
  statement form counts as a write. Declining costs a program an answer it was getting wrong; standing on a
  writable name costs somebody an interrupt they cannot send.
- **Measure the parent build's answer; do not infer it from the code you deleted.** My own comment said `not v`
  over a pair-carrying parameter "died naming the missing tagged value word" before the fix, because the old
  road lowered the operand through the one-word value door. The pre-change binary answered `False` at exit 0 —
  a wrong number, not a refusal. Same for the two `and` shapes and the ternary arm: identical on the baseline,
  which is the difference between filing them as new rows and claiming them as this row's residue. Anything I
  had written from reasoning alone got rewritten after `gustyc_base` was asked beside `gustyc_new`.
- **A row's `Free text` is prose the guards do not read.** `pkg/lang/golden_artifact_counts_test.go` recomputes
  the artifact counts and `roadmap_snapshot_test.go` recomputes the Snapshot table, but a number written inside
  a row's own sentence ("wrote **92** entries") is checked by nobody. The true figure was 98 — my harvest
  predicted 91, the ladder is 6 positions × 15 kinds + the row program = 91, and the extra 7 are the residue and
  conformance programs the same two suites assert. Every count I wrote in the ADR, README and roadmap got
  re-derived from the artifact, and the snapshot guard independently caught four more I had not touched at all
  (ADRs 383→384, programs 236→237, matrix 223→224, oracle `match` 179→180, owed 166→…).
- **An orphan check on the record has to regenerate the programs.** A naive scan for record keys among Go string
  literals reported 78 orphans of 98 — the ladder's programs are built by concatenating a body template with an
  entry, so they exist nowhere as one literal. Rebuilding the 90 combinations in the checker dropped the count to
  0. A tool that cannot express how a test constructs its source will "find" missing coverage that is not
  missing.
- **File the residue as rows, not as sentences.** Four rows went into the Open queue with today's bytes beside
  the reference's — the stale tag and its non-terminating loop (**R.366**), the operand `and`/`or` and the
  ternary choose, which prints an empty list's heap handle where CPython prints `z` (**R.367**), the
  text-returning convention whose parameters never get a second word (**R.368**, which inherited the `str(v)`
  pin that had been riding under R.361), and the empty container spelled as a `list()` stored in a dict literal,
  whose store never asked ADR 0391's door (**R.369**). Each pin fails by AGREEMENT, which is how a paid row is
  supposed to announce itself; `TestARebindingParameterLoopStillRunsForever` passes only if the run is killed.
- **The debt ledger fails on the fix, and that is the feature.** `integration/dict_entry_call_test.go` and
  `pkg/lang/dict_entry_call_test.go` both went red the moment R.361 was answered, because their text says a row
  that agrees with the reference must be deleted; the row left `cpython-debt.json` (10 → 9) with them. A pin that
  survives its own fix is the thing to distrust.
- **Somebody else was editing this working tree.** `AGENTS.md`, `docs/operations.md`, `roadmap.md`, the conformance
  matrix and both debt files changed at minutes when I was not writing them (a second agent on the same row, same
  checkout: `node ./pi-loop.mjs … --force-reset` up 1h06m). The rule I applied: verify a foreign edit against the
  artifact and the tests before touching it — three of their claims were right and kept (the relabelling of the
  `str(v)` pin, the 20-second hang witness, the decline-not-refuse framing) and three were wrong and corrected (the
  entry count, "the ternary arm refuses", "five positions"). Never revert what you have not measured, and never
  trust what you have not measured either.

## ADR 0394 — the pair scan asks the door the roads that store and decide a slot already ask (Gap R.369, 2026-10-22)

- **A wrong answer does not say which road dropped the word.** `d = {"k": list()}` / `f(d["k"])` printed `3`,
  and the row filed against it said the dict-literal store never asked ADR 0391's door. `--emit-llvm` says the
  store asks it fine — `@rt_dict_put_tagged(i32 %…, i32 4, i32 5)`, the tag of a list beside the handle. The
  word was dropped two roads earlier, in the scan that decides whether the read of a slot crosses a call as a
  pair at all: `pairSlotIsSpelling` is a hand-written list of AST node types and a `*Call` is not on it. The
  same `3` is the outside of both stories. Read the IR of the whole crossing before naming a culprit; the row's
  `Item` cell had to be rewritten to say what was actually found, and the "so the hole is in the STORE" clause
  is kept in the file with a strike-through in prose ("the filing guessed the store, and the filing was wrong")
  rather than edited out — the next agent needs to know that a plausible diagnosis sat in the tracker for a day.
- **Three copies of one question is a count, not a coincidence.** ADR 0391 fixed the road that LABELS a slot,
  ADR 0392 the roads that DECIDE a kind, this row the road that decides whether the read crosses. Each of the
  three had re-derived "is this slot self-describing?" from its own AST switch, and each was found by a
  different program. ADR 0232's "one question, one asking place" is the thing to check for the next feature,
  not the thing to cite after the fact.
- **A guard copied from a door must be measured against the door, in both directions.** The scan has no
  `irGen`, so `builtinShadowed` could not be borrowed and had to be re-implemented as `programDefinesName`. The
  first census counted every binding form (`for` variables, another function's parameters), and that is
  *stricter* than the door it copies — which sounds safe and is not: `def g(list): return list` above
  `d = {"k": list()}` / `f(d["k"])` then printed `3` while the emitter went on labelling the entry a container.
  A decline the emitter contradicts is worse than no decline, because the two roads now disagree in public. Both
  directions are pinned in `TestTheEmptyContainerArgumentRoadDeclinesWhatItCannotPromise`: `def set(): return 1`
  must keep the program's own `1`, and an unrelated parameter named `list` must not take the spelling.
- **A decline that still emits the pair road is a half-open door, so assert the absence.** The shadowing
  controls do not only check the printed bytes; they read the callee's body and fail if `%_v_tag` or
  `@rt_dict_get_tagged` is present. Without that, a "decline" that emits the pair anyway and prints right by
  luck looks identical to a decline.
- **Ask the caller's region for the caller's call.** Two IR asserts failed for a reason that was purely about
  which region was read: `@rt_dict_get_tagged` / `@rt_dict_value_tag` are lowered in the caller's `@main`, while
  `@rt_pair_truth` and `%_v_tag` live in the callee. Asking the callee for the first pair reported a missing ask
  that was sitting one region away. Every IR claim now says whose body it reads.
- **A probe harness reports its own bugs as regressions.** The before/after sweep first printed "9 REGRESSED".
  The reference leg had been invoked as `python3 --file /tmp/prN.gy` — an argument error on every program — so
  "agrees with the reference" had degraded to "both failed the same way". Fixed the harness, the 9 regressions
  became 0 and the honest number appeared: 7 → 34 agreeing over 46 probes, 27 newly. From now on the harness is
  validated on a program I already know prints correctly before any count it produces is believed.
- **`grep` the identifier; do not remember it.** Several hours went into reasoning about `pairCallTarget`,
  `pairCallInfo`, `pairTagIsDynamic` and a per-call-site `allExcluded` escape, none of which exist in this repo.
  They were plausible shapes imported from how I would have written the pass, and the prose built on them was
  internally consistent and completely false. `grep -rn pairCallTarget pkg/lang` returns nothing and takes four
  seconds. Any claim about a mechanism now has the grep that backs it, and every comment in the diff names a
  function I have seen with my own eyes in the file.
- **The multi-site hazard was there before I got to it, and got easier to stand on.** A callee's pair layout is
  chosen from one call site and reused, so `f(list(), 5)` then `f(1, 2)` prints `[] 2`. It is not this row's
  doing — `f([1], 2)` / `f(3, 4)` prints `[] 4` on the parent build too — but `[]`, `{}` and `set()` are
  spellings now, so the mixed shape went from exotic to ordinary. Measured on the parent before filing, filed as
  **Gap R.374** with both reproducers and the scan data structure (`calls[fn][i]`) a fix needs, and the
  conformance program was written to avoid the shape rather than to hide it: the omission is said out loud in
  the details file.
- **Two pins deleted, not rewritten.** `an_empty_container_written_as_a_call_crosses_as_an_integer` and
  `the_set_spelling_of_the_same_entry` left both residue tables (package and CLI) and went into the answering
  ladders. A pin that survives its own fix is the thing to distrust; the note about where they went is in the
  surviving table's doc comment, not welded onto a row that no longer describes them.
- **A conformance program is a negotiation with the current backend.** Getting `programs/empty_container_argument.gy`
  to print CPython's 55 lines took four cuts: `len(xs)` over a mixed list hits Gap R.82's refusal; a second
  `xs =` in a function body collides with the module-level `xs` in the scan's per-name binding table and refuses
  the whole file; `xs = [v]` inside the callee is Gap R.371; two call sites of one callee with different
  argument shapes is Gap R.374. Every one is a filed row, and each cut is a probe that belongs to that row's
  pin rather than to this program — the program is what the backend answers today, not what it should answer.

## ADR 0395 — an entry lambda is minted with the words it reads; the clone supplies them (Gap R.336, 2026-10-22)

- **A refusal can be true about the value and wrong about the caller.** The pass declined this family with
  "an entry is a bare symbol with no environment to carry", and that sentence is correct — ADR 0345 §1 makes
  an entry a `define`. It just does not apply, because an entry is not called from anywhere the program can
  point at: it is called by the CLONE, from a body the pass writes, and the pass had the host frame in hand
  the whole time (`entryHost` is the table that already decides whose locals an entry's reads resolve
  through). When a refusal cites a property of a representation, ask who is standing on the other side of
  that representation before accepting it as a limit.
- **The obstacle the filing feared was already discriminated by a key it owned.** The row was written as
  though the clone's identity would need a second axis: two applications of `apply1` whose entries read
  different names would need two clones. They already get two — `callableClone.key` IS the tuple of entry
  symbols, the body is written out of it (`callee.Fn = cl.key[slot]`), and captures are a property of a
  minted symbol. The rejected alternative is the one that would have re-keyed clones by (symbol, captures):
  more clones, no new discrimination, and a broken `callableCloneNamesDiffer`. Before adding an axis, print
  the keys you have.
- **One question, one door — and this time the second door was deleted, not fed.** `callableLambdaFrameRead`
  (the decline predicate) and `callableLambdaCaptures` (the list ADR 0370 fills) both walk a lambda body
  looking for free names; the plan's decline was asking one of them and the hoist now asks the other, and the
  two had already drifted on nested-lambda bodies and on the module-name rule. The fix keeps the list door and
  demotes the boolean one to what it is actually for — naming the blocking name in the message. This is the
  same lesion ADR 0391, 0392 and 0394 found in the container roads, at the third family of roads.
- **A gate belongs where the facts are, and that is a positional argument.** The clone hands the forwarded
  word to the entry POSITIONALLY and the hoisted entry carries no `Captures` field. `Captures` is the
  instruction "the caller reaches for this name by name", and the codegen gate that asks whether a name can
  cross as one word (`captureCarriesOneWord`, Gap R.332) is asked of whoever holds it. Put the field on the
  entry and the gate is asked of a minted parameter with no facts of its own — the host's `base` is a local
  with a type in the tables, `%p2` is nothing. The value reaches the entry through the host's read either
  way; only one placement asks the honest question.
- **An all-or-nothing pass needs a narrow loud decline, not a silent rename.** A forwarded word is a
  PARAMETER of the clone. If the higher-order body already owns that name — `def apply1(fn, v): base = 9`
  over `apply1(lambda x: x + base, seed)` — the clone has two slots under one spelling and the body's own
  read answers the forwarded word. Renaming the minted parameter would fix that program and bury the class,
  so the pass says which name is in the way in which body (**Gap R.375**), and the row records the fix's
  shape (mint unspeakably, fill positionally) rather than a shortcut that makes the test green.
- **The account and the terminal can both be honest about different stages.** `gustyc --callables` says
  `rewritten` for the container-capture program because the pass DID rewrite it; codegen then refuses it with
  Gap R.332's one-word sentence. The first cut of the test pinned the pass's `refused` and failed on a
  compile that goes further than the pass. The account reports what the pass did; the refusal reports where
  the program stopped. Two stages, two claims, and only the second one reaches `--file`.
- **The pass's arithmetic has to know about the words it supplies itself.** `callableInnerAgrees` counts the
  arguments the body spells against `plan.arity[entry]`, and `arity` is now the hoisted `define`'s parameter
  count — lambda parameters plus captures. Every forwarded program failed that audit until the comparison
  subtracted `len(plan.entryCaptures[entry])`. A pass that mints parameters has to edit every consumer that
  counts them; the audit that reads `srcParams` (ADR 0372's fix) was the one that already knew.
- **Two stale pins were bugs, not documentation.** `TestWhatTheTruthOfAPairSuppliedParameterStillOwes`
  pinned `an empty container written as a call` as a residue with the wrong bytes, in both the package and the
  CLI table, and the CLI leg was FAILING: ADR 0394 had landed under the same gap and nobody moved the pins.
  A residue row is a claim about today. They were deleted (both tables) and the shapes moved to the answering
  tables; the doc comment now says where they went.
- **Measure a neighbour on the parent before adopting it.** Two probes disagreed at the end of the sweep:
  `sorted(xs, key=lambda …)` inside a def refuses, and a def that RETURNS a keyed sort prints `0`. A build of
  `e101ec5` printed the same refusal and the same `0`. The first is filed as **Gap R.376** (the hook hoists
  by a second road that never asks the door), the second belongs to **Gap R.328** already. Adopting either
  would have made this commit claim a fix it did not make and hide a road it did not widen.
- **Determinism is a property of the plan, not of the emitter.** The forwarded word's name reaches the clone
  through `forwarded`, unioned in tuple order, and the minted names come from a counter whose starting point
  is the plan's own iteration order — so two compiles of one source agree only because the plan walks the
  program once, in order. The IR test re-emits and diffs, which is what would catch a map iteration creeping
  into `entryCaptures`.

## ADR 0396 — the ordering door's hook lambda is minted with the words it reads (Gap R.376, 2026-10-22)

- **Three roads that hoist a `lambda` is three answers to one question, and the third one was the bug.** The
  applied body asks `callableLambdaCaptures` (ADR 0370), the entry asks it too (ADR 0395), and the `key=` hook
  asked `callableLambdaIsSelfContained` — a spelling test that says "any free name: decline". The refused
  program printed a sentence about a representation nobody was using ("a lambda is a function VALUE") because
  the road that decides is not the road that speaks. ADR 0391, 0392 and 0394 each found this lesion in the
  container family; this is the same patient in the callable family, and the tell was identical: a refusal that
  is true about the mechanism and silent about the program. When a feature refuses with a sentence about how
  something is *represented*, grep for who else represents it that way and asks anyway.
- **The gate that decides "is this position a call" already existed, and reusing it is what kept the row
  small.** `keyDoorOptions` (the callee must be `sorted`/`min`/`max`, the option must be `key=`, an unknown
  option means the door raises so there is no call) is read by the door, by the parameter scan (ADR 0363) and
  now by the hoist. The tempting local version — "is this a `key=` keyword argument" — would have hoisted
  `sorted(xs, reverse=lambda …)` with capture words no call ever fills, and minted parameters for a lambda in a
  position the door never calls. One census, three readers.
- **A `Captures` field is an instruction, so its meaning is the caller, not the field.** The entry road leaves
  `Captures` empty and is filled positionally because its caller is a clone the pass wrote; the hook road sets
  it, because its caller is a frame of the program and reaching for the name by name is exactly what the source
  means. Same minting, opposite choice, decided by who is standing on the other side of the call — the second
  time ADR 0395's lesson about a refusal citing a property of a representation has come up. If two roads agree
  on the representation and disagree on the caller, they should disagree in the code.
- **A minted parameter is invisible to every arity census that counts `def.Params`.** The hook's declaration
  has two parameters and the door supplies one, so the key door raised `<lambda>() missing 1 required
  positional argument: 'base'` for a program that wrote no argument, and `keyDoorCallsOneArgument` answered
  "never called" — which is worse than wrong, because `callableNoFunctionValuesLeft` reads an uncalled key as a
  function value left in the program and hands the whole program to the ordinary road. Two doors, one number,
  and the fix is a door (`callableSuppliedParams`) rather than two `if len(fd.Captures) > 0` guards. The
  `Default`-on-the-minted-parameter trick would have passed every test in the row and made "omittable" mean two
  things; the decision row that asks the census directly (`TestTheHookDoorCountsOnlyTheArgumentsTheSourceSupplies`,
  with a two-argument key as its negative control) is what makes the difference falsifiable.
- **A refusal that MOVES is a finding, not a detail.** Three shapes this row newly hoists then refused with a
  *better* sentence than the key door's: a text or container capture reaches Gap R.332's one-word rule, float
  elements reach Gap R.248's, a module `for` target reaches Gap R.35's. Each was measured on the parent (still
  exit 1, still a refusal) and recorded as a move rather than filed as a fix; a table that only says
  "refused, unchanged" would have hidden the fact that the row made four diagnostics more honest by making the
  program reach the door that owns the missing half.
- **Two stages, two claims, again — and this time the account was the confusing one.** For
  `sorted(…, key=lambda s: s + label)` the pass reports `capture_parameters: 1` and the emitter refuses,
  because the frame owns `label` (so one word is needed) and the value behind it is a text (so one i32 cannot
  carry it). The row first asserted 0 for that program and failed on 1. The account reports what the pass did;
  only the later verdict reaches `--file` — which is the ADR 0395 lesson, re-collected with a counter-example
  instead of a restatement.
- **A pre-existing wrapper is a reason to file, not to route around.** `noteUnlowered`'s `Stmt` arm prefixes
  `codegen: a *lang.ExprStmt statement cannot be compiled:` to a refusal, and three refusal rows in this one
  commit needed to strip it to assert anything about the sentence underneath. That is the third copy-of-a-rule
  tell in reverse: when N guards all carve out the same exception, the exception is a row. Filed as **Gap
  R.377** with its DoD written as "the three strips are deleted", measured byte-identical on the parent, and
  the *tempting* two-line fix left out of this commit because the statement's Python-facing name is a
  diagnostic design decision and this commit is about a call.
- **A guard rail made a refusal honest before it made it green.** The first cut of the module-level hook let
  `key=lambda x: helper(x)` hoist with a capture for a module-level `def` name, which is a parameter filled
  from `%_helper` — a slot that does not exist, because a function is declared rather than assigned (ADR 0345
  §1). Left in, that program would have printed a plausible number at exit 0. `callableCapturesAreValueNames`
  declines it and the shape stays the door's refusal, filed as **Gap R.378** with the reproducer and the
  shadowing question that makes the real fix a row rather than two lines. Declining is cheap; a wrong answer at
  exit 0 is the expensive bug this file keeps saying so about.
- **The before/after sweep is only as good as its reference leg — validated first, then trusted.** The sweep
  runs every probe through `python3` and calls a program AGREED only when the binary exits 0 *and* its stdout
  equals the reference's byte for byte; the harness refuses to produce a count until a known-good program prints
  correctly through it (the ADR 0394 lesson, applied without being re-derived). 26 probes: 5 agreeing on
  `e101ec5`'s successor, 22 on this build, 17 newly, 0 regressed. Two probes were dropped for reasons the
  harness surfaced rather than hid: one is a front-end parse limitation (`str(len(s) + base)`), and one — a
  `def` that RETURNS a keyed sort — prints `0` on both builds and belongs to **Gap R.328**, so adopting it would
  have been this commit claiming a fix it did not make.
- **A conformance program is a negotiation, and the negotiation is written down.** The row's file avoids the
  shapes the backend does not answer today (a hook reading a frame two steps out, a container or text capture, a
  run-time-built container, two call sites of one callee with different argument shapes) and says so in a
  comment naming the rows, because a program that quietly omits them reads as coverage. The module-level
  `for`-target probe stayed OUT of the program for the same reason: it refuses with Gap R.35's sentence, and a
  matrix row is a claim about what prints, not about what is interesting.

## ADR 0397 — the word a clone forwards to its entry is minted; the host still reads the name the program wrote (Gap R.375, 2026-10-22)

- **A decline can be a naming bug wearing a semantics costume.** ADR 0395's `already owns that name` decline was
  true about the representation and wrong about the language: fourteen programs the reference answers were standing
  behind it, and the thing the body "already owned" was a slot the compiler had invented. The tell was in the
  ADR's own sentence — *the word the clone would forward is a name the body reads for itself* — which names a
  parameter nobody in the program can see. When a decline explains itself with a name the source never wrote, ask
  who chose that name; the answer here was "me, one cycle ago, to make a keyword fill findable".
- **One string doing three jobs is the defect; separate the jobs before arguing about the fix.** The captured
  spelling was simultaneously the host's read, the clone's parameter and the entry's parameter — and only the
  middle one belonged to the pass. Writing the three-column table (who reads it / whose tables know the value) made
  the design forced: two of the names are program text and cannot move, so mint the third. The same table is why
  the two gates stayed where they were: each is asked of a *named frame*, and a frame is not a string.
- **The filing's mechanism was measured and rejected.** Gap R.375's "next concrete action" said fill the minted
  word **positionally** at the application. It is not safe here, for a reason the row's own neighbour owns: an
  application may leave parameters out (**Gap R.329**, ADR 0371), the positional list stops at the last dispatched
  position, and the call road fills the rest from each parameter's `Default` — so an appended word lands in a
  default's slot. And the fill is where `captureCarriesOneWord` is asked with the supplying frame on the tables and
  where the verdict is recorded; moving the argument into the tree moves it out of that door, which is the same
  reasoning ADR 0395 §4 used to deny the hoisted entry a `Captures` field. A roadmap suggestion is a hypothesis
  written before the code was read; landing it without re-testing it is how a filing becomes a bug report.
- **Ask "where is the gate asked?", not "does the test go green?".** The tempting one-field change was to let the
  pass write the argument and delete the emitter's fill. Every answering probe stayed green. What caught it is a
  probe whose ONLY purpose is to make the two frames disagree: the host holds `base = "hey"` while the higher-order
  body holds `base = 9`. Asked of the host, the gate refuses (Gap R.332, the honest answer); asked of the clone, the
  program compiles and prints a number — an exit-0 wrong answer, the class this file keeps saying is expensive.
  Every gate needs at least one probe where the two candidate frames disagree, or the gate's location is untested.
- **A new accessor has to answer for every frame that exists, not just the one the row introduced.**
  `callableCaptureRead(fd, i)` first returned `""` when `fd` was unknown, and the frames that broke were the
  emitter's own inline lambdas — minted by `emitLambda`, absent from `g.fds`, and never supposed to have a
  forwarded word at all. `print((lambda x: (lambda y: (lambda z: x + y + z)(100))(10))(1))`, the Gap R.330 control,
  went from `111` to a refusal in the first sweep. The fix was a fallback to the parameter's own spelling; the lesson
  is that "the field is empty" and "the field does not apply to this shape" are different answers, and the fallback
  has to be the second one spelled out. Keeping ADR 0395's and ADR 0372's programs in the probe set is what turned
  that from a released regression into a five-minute fix.
- **The recursion is the one call whose caller is not a frame of the program.** For every application the host
  reaches for its own name; for a clone's self call the caller is a frame that owns nothing, so the pass writes the
  fill itself and hands the parameter down. That asymmetry — not the minting — is the part of this row with real
  content, and it is ADR 0385's rule for the entry tuple applied one word taller. The IR claim that proves it is
  `…(i32 %t15, i32 0, i32 %p2)`: the recursive call's last operand is the clone's own parameter register, and no
  `%_base` load appears in it while the clone's own `store i32 100, i32* %_base` survives beside it.
- **Two stages, two claims — the account disagreed with my arithmetic again.** For
  `(lambda fn: fn(2) + shift + step)(lambda n: n * step)` I wrote `capture_parameters: 2` — one body capture plus
  the minted word. The pass reported 3: the body reads `shift` AND `step`, so ADR 0372 writes two words and this row
  writes one. The account reports what the pass wrote onto the declaration; only the later verdict reaches
  `--file`. Third cycle, same lesson, new counter-example.
- **A parameter register is positional in the IR, so an AST-level minting is invisible there — and that is the
  point.** IR claims cannot see `gy$cap$…` (parameters print as `%p0`), and they must not: ADR 0345 §3 keeps the
  pass's private spellings out of anything a reader or an agent parses. The minting is therefore asserted where
  the name exists — against the plan itself, in an in-package test — and the IR asserts the consequence instead
  (the entry call's operands are `%p` registers, never `%_base`). Assert a fact at the layer where it is
  representable, and add the leak guard in the same commit: the minted spelling forbidden from the module and from
  every refusal.
- **Guards over artifacts are the reason the docs stayed true without effort.** `tools/recmerge` wrote 38 entries and
  the record moved to 8525; the next test run named the four numbers in `roadmap.md` and `docs/operations.md` that
  had gone stale, plus the matrix and oracle counts, none of which I had thought to count. The conformance program
  was accepted by CPython on the first try and became a matrix row (`programs/forwarded_word`) with its own
  `testdata/forwarded_word.expected`, written by the reference and never by this backend.
- **Two IR-assertion traps, both cheap and both hit.** Matching the word `call` inside a clone region matches the
  word `callable` in the clone's own `define` line — match `= call ` and skip `define`s. And a probe that reads a
  name two frames out has to be written in dependency order: my first version put the callee's `def` after its use
  and got the front end's `undefined name` instead of the pass's sentence, which would have pinned the wrong row.
- **Tool flakiness is a correctness hazard, not an annoyance.** Reads and edits intermittently returned nothing or
  an error while the file on disk was fine. The countermeasure is the same one the suite applies to itself: never
  trust an empty result as evidence about state — re-check with `git diff --stat` after an edit and `gofmt` +
  `go build` before believing a file is what I think it is.

## ADR 0398 — a statement's refusal is the door's own sentence, at the frame and line the program wrote it (Gap R.377, 2026-10-22)

- **A workaround that has been promoted into the suite is the loudest bug report the suite can produce.** The
  evidence for this row was not a wrong answer; it was two lines of Go in the rows that shipped a cycle earlier —
  `if m := regexp.MustCompile("^codegen: a \\*lang\\.[A-Za-z]+Stmt statement cannot be compiled: ")…; said = said[len(m):]`
  in `pkg/lang/key_hook_frame_test.go` and its `integration` twin. A leak-guards test that removes a leak before
  looking for a leak is not testing anything, and the moment a suite adapts to a leak, CI goes green on top of it.
  Deleting those two carve-outs and asserting the wrapper's ABSENCE is what turned the row from cosmetics into a
  guard. Read your own tests for `TrimPrefix`, allowlists and `(?:^|: )?`-style optional prefixes: each is a defect
  with the serial numbers filed off.
- **A diagnostic's two audiences are the same bytes, so fix them together or not at all.** `--json` carries the
  emitter's `error` string verbatim, so the same `*lang.ExprStmt` was the string an agent might branch on. What
  changed for the machine was nothing — `phase`, `exit` and `capability.code` are computed from the payload, which is
  exactly why removing the wrapper was safe — and what changed for the human was the whole message. Pin both channels
  in the same commit (`TestTheMachinePathStillClassesAStatementRefusal` asserts the CLI sentence and the JSON document
  in one run) or the two will drift the way the pre-ADR-0346 prose did.
- **"Is this payload already a sentence?" was a question the toolchain could answer instead of guess.** The tempting
  implementation was a `refusalError` Go type threaded through ~142 `codegen:` refusal sites — a diff to code that
  decides programs, and quietly defeatable by forgetting the type at one site. ADR 0346 had already rejected that
  shape for the same reason, and the classifier it built (`ClassifyCapabilityRefusal`, the one `--capabilities` and
  `--json` read) plus ADR 0166's "a refusal cites its row" rule answer the question with no new type and no new
  invariant to rot. Side effect worth naming: a refusal that does NOT cite its row and is unknown to the registry now
  arrives wrapped in ``the `return` at line 6 cannot be compiled:``, which is a mild pressure toward citing.
- **A sentence some other file quotes verbatim is load-bearing whether or not it reads well.** The obvious refactor
  was to fold the `*FuncDef` arm into the new passthrough — `*FuncDef` implements `Stmt`, so `where.(Stmt)` catches
  it, and the result would have been green on every test I wrote until I remembered the drift ledger.
  `testdata/interpreter-golden-drift.json` quotes Gap R.38's `function "m" cannot be compiled:` in two rows, and a
  drift row whose wording changes under `TestMain` is a divergence that *silently disappeared* — the one failure the
  ratchet is built to make loud. So the exclusion is in code, with a comment, and in a byte-for-byte test
  (`TestTheFuncDefArmStillNamesTheFunction`). Before deleting any wording anywhere, grep the artifacts for it.
- **The fallback arm of a helper is the arm that regresses, so it gets a case.** `stmtSurface`'s default answers
  ``the statement at line 41`` for a `Stmt` implementation the language cannot write, and nothing in the compiler
  reaches it today — which is precisely why it needed a witness. The test invents one (`oddStmt`, a local type
  implementing `stmtNode()`/`Span()`) plus the `nil` input. Same reasoning for the wrapper arm: `refusalIsSentence`
  is tested with its negative control, a raw helper error, because a passthrough that also swallowed raw payloads
  would pass every family case and lose the subject of the sentence.
- **Never rewrite a golden artifact by hand.** I ran a Python round-trip over
  `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden.json` to deduplicate two entries I had pasted in, and rewrote 55,838 lines —
  the file is a MAP keyed by source, my script treated `entries` as a list, and `json.dump` reformatted every entry in
  it. `git checkout` saved the row. The record is written by `tools/recmerge` or not at all, and the check that a
  record-writing was surgical is `git diff --numstat` on the artifact: nine entries is 42 lines, not 64,000.
- **A "before" column has to be a build, and the "after" build has to be rebuilt.** Two failures in one measurement
  round, both silent: the probe script called a `/tmp` CLI built earlier in the session, so the "after" column was
  the "before" build and reported six leaks still present; and the parent build came from a `git stash` of a dirty
  tree rather than a `git worktree add --detach /tmp/… HEAD`, so it was one edit away from containing the fix. Now:
  `go worktree` + `go build -o /tmp/gustyc-base ./cmd/gustyc` for the parent, an explicit rebuild of the worktree
  binary before every probe run, and a harness that refuses to produce a count until a known-good program prints
  correctly through it (ADR 0394's lesson, third cycle of being re-derived instead of remembered).
- **File the leaks you find while measuring, in a table that fails when somebody fixes them.** The same probe round
  turned up three more `%T` leaks behind other doors (`… got *lang.ListLit`, `unsupported assignment target
  *lang.Attr`, the parser's `(got *lang.IntLit)`). Fixing them here would have been a second feature in one commit and
  a roadmap row nobody wrote; ignoring them would have lost them. So: **Gap R.379** as an OPEN row, a section in
  `docs/roadmap-details.md`, and `TestWhatTheRowLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed`, which asserts the leaked text is
  PRESENT and fails when it is absent, saying "move this row to DONE and delete the pin". A pin that fails on
  improvement is worth more than a TODO.
- **Two ADR files cannot share a number, and only a guard will tell you.** `docs/adr/0398-…md` was already there when
  I wrote mine — the same decision, written before a context break — and the count guard caught it
  (`the ADRs row says 388 records; the artifact says 390`, with the highest number still `0398`). The fix was to keep
  the better-developed file, correct its numbers against this round's actual measurement (its before-column cited the
  grandparent commit, and its record count was three entries behind), and delete the duplicate. `git status docs/adr`
  before writing an ADR, and believe the artifact-count guards when they contradict your memory.

## ADR 0399 — a hook that calls a function the module declares gets the call by symbol (Gap R.378, 2026-10-22)

- **A second opinion asked after the shared door is the defect, and the sibling roads are the evidence.** The hook
  road called `callableLambdaCaptures` and then overrode it with `callableCapturesAreValueNames`. The applied road and
  the entry road call the same door with no override, and had been answering the shape (`(lambda x: helper(x) + 5)(3)`
  → `2`) for cycles. When one of three callers of a helper disagrees with the other two, fix the caller that
  special-cases, not the helper — and go read the other two before writing anything. ADR 0232's lesion keeps
  reappearing at whatever the newest road is.
- **Distinguish occurrences by NODE, never by spelling, when one identifier can play two roles.**
  `key=lambda x: helper(x) + len(str(helper))` mentions `helper` twice with two different answers: a call the hoisted
  `define` can emit, and a value read that has no word. A `map[string]bool` of names cannot express the difference; a
  `map[*Name]bool` of callee positions collected by the walker can. `callableFreeNameSet(l, skip)` exists for exactly
  that, and `callableFreeNames` became a wrapper over it so the census still exists once.
- **The row's real number is the "wrong answer" column, not the "newly agreeing" column.** 23 programs came over to
  the reference's side; the number I actually defended is **0 programs where the compiled leg prints what CPython does
  not**, over 16 probes written to attack the new gate rather than flatter it (`helper = 3` after the call, inside a
  module-level `if`, inside a module-level `for`, an alias `alias = helper`, a method callee, a callee that mutates a
  module list, a `def` declared in a conditional block). Write the attacking half FIRST: a gate widened to answer more
  programs is only safe if the shapes it cannot see keep refusing.
- **The conservative version of an ordering rule is chosen by the REPRESENTATION, not by taste.** The hooked hook is a
  `define` that reaches `helper` by symbol, so it can never see a slot — which means the correct answer to "may I
  hoist this hook, given the module might rebind the name" is "no", whatever the analysis says about whether the
  rebind runs first. Both conservative rules (declaration above the hook; no rebind anywhere at module level) are one
  comparison each and can never fabricate. A cleverer dataflow version buys nothing and risks the worst class in this
  file: a plausible handle at the exit code of success.
- **Frame ownership has to be one function, because the shadow question and the capture question are the same
  question.** `callableFrameOwns` came out of `callableLambdaCaptures`'s own body rather than being written beside the
  new gate. If I had written a second census of "what does this frame bind", the two would have disagreed about
  `for`/`with`/comprehension targets within a cycle, and the disagreement would have shown up as a program that
  printed the module's function where the reference raises `TypeError`.
- **Never hand-type an expectation into an answer table — and make the record leg fail on a MISSING entry so the
  hand-typed ones cannot survive.** Three of my 28 family rows were written from memory instead of from `python3`; the
  record test caught all three (`want: "8"` for a program whose answer is `2`, and two answered programs that were not
  on the record at all). The failing-on-absence rule is what turns the record into a witness at this altitude rather
  than an ornament.
- **A stale measurement file can manufacture a bug report.** Between probe rounds I read `measure.json` produced by an
  earlier run and "found" three wrong answers from the new gate. They were the previous cycle's rows. Now a measurement
  round regenerates its own JSON, names it after the round, and prints the harness sanity line (`N go-family programs
  print the reference answer through this harness`) beside the counts; a count with no sanity line beside it is
  unread. Same lesson about binaries: rebuild the "after" build immediately before the run, and take the "before"
  build from `git worktree add --detach … HEAD`, never from a stash.
- **One careless multi-region edit nearly cost a function.** An edit intended to delete dead code
  (`callableNameIsCalledOnly`) matched through the following function's signature and left a duplicate
  `callableCalleeNameNodes` with `callableDisplayNameOf`'s body glued to it. `go build` caught it in five seconds, so
  the rule is not "be careful with `edit`" but "build after every surgical edit that spans function boundaries, and
  `grep -n` the names you touched". Deleting dead code is only worth it if the deletion is verified.
- **Adding a conformance program moves five snapshot numbers at once, and only the guards know which.** Registering
  `programs/hook_named_call.gy` changed `Conformance programs`, `Matrix rows` (both cells), `Oracle verdicts`,
  `Retired-engine record` and `Rows owed`, plus the ADR count and the record count quoted in `AGENTS.md` and
  `docs/operations.md`. `TestTheRoadmapSnapshotIsMeasuredNotRemembered` and the two artifact-count tests name every
  cell and both numbers; the workflow is to let them fail first and edit what they name, rather than hunting for
  sentences to edit and missing the one nobody reads.
- **Pin a refusal's absence from the capability registry too.** The key road's `a lambda is a function VALUE` sentence
  is classified as nothing today. Instead of asserting nothing, the decline table carries a `code` field whose empty
  string means "the registry answers nothing", so the day someone registers a code for it the table fails and gets
  read (ADR 0346's contract is that an agent branches on these codes — a code appearing, vanishing or moving is a
  branch silently stopping firing).
- **`gustyc --emit-llvm` takes the SOURCE as its value** (`--emit-llvm="<src>"`, with `--opt-level=0` before it, per
  `cmd/gustyc/main_test.go`). Three probe rounds were spent on a flag that was silently consuming the filename and
  printing an empty `main`. When an interface behaves implausibly, read the CLI's own test for the calling convention
  before guessing twice.

## ADR 0400 — the doors that refuse an assignment target name the node the program wrote (Gap R.379, 2026-10-23)

- **A guard written to fail when a defect is fixed is a better tracker than an issue.** The three `%T` leaks this row
  closed were pinned by `TestWhatTheRowLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed`, which asserts the leaked text is PRESENT and
  fails when it is absent. When I made the fix the test failed exactly as designed — “Gap R.379 has been closed — the
  leaked `*lang.ListLit` no longer appears, so move this row to DONE and delete the pin” — and the failure text told me
  which two tables to edit. A TODO would have rotted; a pin that fails on improvement cannot.
- **Before rewording anything, grep the artifacts for the string.** The same door family included
  `unsupported attr expression`, one line from being fixable. `grep` found it quoted verbatim by four rows of
  `pkg/lang/testdata/interpreter-golden-drift.json`, by `dead_binding_test.go` and by the CLI's exit-code table — so
  rewording it would have made four recorded divergences silently disappear, which is the failure class ADR 0398 says
  this suite fears most. The row stopped at the three sites whose sentences nothing quotes, left the fourth to
  **Gap R.272** (whose definition of done already asks for it), and pinned the current wording with a test that
  explains the ledger duty in its own failure text. “Check the artifacts” is a five-second habit with a four-row
  payoff.
- **A shared door is only shared if its fallback is safe.** `exprSurface` was the obvious thing to reuse, and its
  fallback is `fmt.Sprintf("a %T", e)` — perfect for the messages ADR 0386 built it for, and a direct route back to the
  Go type name for a refusal whose entire claim is that it names the program. `nodeSurface` shares the rendering and
  owns the fallback (“an expression the compiler cannot name”), with a test-local `oddExpr` giving the fallback arm a
  witness. Reusing a helper is not reusing its failure mode.
- **Kind before rendering.** Naming an attribute target by its formatter text produced ``the attribute `1.x``` — a
  string that appears in no source file — because `(1).x` renders through the shared expression printer. The fix was to
  name the attribute and then say what it hangs off: ``the attribute `x` of a number``. A diagnostic should contain
  pieces the reader can point at, and “the number `3`” beats `*lang.IntLit` for the same reason “a number” beats `int`
  in a Python traceback.
- **One container representation, two spellings, one diagnostic consequence.** A tuple literal is a `*ListLit` with a
  flag (ADR 0361). A door that prints “the list literal” for `(1, 2)` has just contradicted the language's own
  semantics in the sentence that tells someone what to fix — so the flag decides the noun, and the parentheses are
  re-rendered because the canonical formatter prints the shared `[…]` shape. Every door that *reads* a container asks
  the flag; this row is the reminder that every door that *names* one has to as well.
- **The control leg finds bugs; that is what it is for.** Six “unchanged behaviour” controls were written to prove the
  row moved no verdict, and one of them (`def bump(c): c.v += 3`) turned out to be the reference's `3` and our
  `unsupported attr expression` — a divergence that was on no record (the recorder refuses an entry the compiled leg
  won't agree to) and pinned nowhere. It is pinned now, with the reference's answer in the table. When a control
  disagrees, the control is the finding.
- **Ask CPython what it does with your own refusal table — the column is a gap-finder.** The 16 shapes were written to
  cover node kinds, and I expected the reference column to be decoration. It split the family in two: 11 refusals CPython
  agrees with, and 5 programs it answers (`xs[0] += 5` → `6`, and four item stores through a container that is not a
  variable → `1`/`[3]`). Rewording a refusal the reference does not share buys nothing at all, so the row stopped at the
  sentence and filed **Gap R.380** and **Gap R.381** instead — both cited from inside the new sentences and pinned against
  live CPython in both legs. The roadmap gained two rows from a wording cycle, and neither of them was invented.
- **Extract the probe list from the tests, don't retype it.** My first probe family “measured” zero leaks, because the
  shapes I had typed from memory never reached the doors — `print(1)(2)` is not an assignment, `[1, 2][0] = 9` reaches the
  item store only because the parser admits an `Index` target, and a `:=` spelling CPython rejects can never be on the
  record. The final harness parses the Go tables for `src`/`said`/`cites` and drives those, so the measured population is
  the asserted population. Print the parent build's message for at least one probe before believing any before-count —
  `16 leaks, 0 after` is only worth anything if the 16 were leaking.
- **A wording cycle moves no verdicts and still owes the record its controls.** I wrote “`tools/recmerge` wrote 0
  entries” into the ADR, the README and the roadmap row, and `git status` then said the golden file was modified: the five
  controls had never been asked in those exact spellings, so recmerge had added all five (8563 → 8568). The claim that
  survives is the narrower one — no *refusal* is on the record, and `TestTheTargetFormsTheReferenceAnswersAreOnTheRecord`
  asserts the sixteen refusals are absent — and the general rule is that an artifact claim gets written after the
  artifact is diffed, never after the run is remembered.
- **A blank line inside a markdown table is a data-loss bug.** Inserting two rows above `## Phase tables` put them below
